title.zh: 卷四百七十四 列傳第二百三十三 姦臣四 万俟禼 韓侂胄 丁大全 賈似道
title.en: Volume 474 Biographies 233: Treacherous Officials 4 - Wan Sixie, Han Tuozhou, Ding Daquan, Jia Sidao
title.raw: 卷四百七十四 列傳第二百三十三 姦臣四 万俟禼 韓侂胄 丁大全 賈似道 Volume 474 Biographies 233: Treacherous Officials 4 - Wan Sixie, Han Tuozhou, Ding Daquan, Jia Sidao

sentences.zh: 万俟禼 韓侂胄 丁大全 賈似道

translations.literal: Wan Sijie, Han Tuozhou, Ding Daquan, Jia Sidao
translations.idiomatic: Wan Sijie, Han Tuozhou, Ding Daquan, and Jia Sidao

sentences.zh: 万俟禼

translations.literal: Wan Sijie
translations.idiomatic: Wan Sijie

sentences.zh: 万俟禼字元忠，開封陽武縣人。

translations.literal: Wan Sijie, style name Yuanzhong, was a native of Yangwu County in Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Wan Sijie, whose style name was Yuanzhong, came from Yangwu County in Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 登政和二年上舍第。

translations.literal: He passed the upper-division examination in the second year of the Zhenghe reign.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenghe (1112), he passed the upper-division examination at the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 調相州、潁昌府教授，曆太學錄、樞密院編修官、尚書比部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was assigned as professor at Xiangzhou and Yingchang Prefecture, and successively served as recorder of the Imperial University, compiler at the Bureau of Military Affairs, and vice director of the Ministry of Revenue's comparison bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as professor at Xiangzhou and Yingchang Prefecture, then served in turn as recorder of the Imperial University, compiler at the Bureau of Military Affairs, and vice director in the Ministry of Revenue's comparison bureau.

sentences.zh: 紹興初，盜曹成掠荊湖間，禼時避亂沅、湘，帥臣程昌寓以便宜檄禼權沅州事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Shaoxing reign, the bandit Cao Cheng plundered the Jinghu region. Sijie was then avoiding turmoil in Yuan and Xiang, and the commander Cheng Changyu issued him a discretionary commission to act as temporary administrator of Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shaoxing era, the bandit Cao Cheng ravaged the Jinghu region. Sijie had fled the turmoil to Yuan and Xiang, where the regional commander Cheng Changyu gave him discretionary authority to govern Yuanzhou on a provisional basis.

sentences.zh: 成奄至城下，禼召土豪、集丁壯以守，成食盡乃退。

translations.literal: Cheng suddenly arrived beneath the city walls. Sijie summoned local magnates and gathered able-bodied men to defend; when Cheng's provisions were exhausted he withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cheng suddenly appeared before the walls, Sijie rallied local strongmen and mustered fighting men for the defense. Cao withdrew only after his supplies ran out.

sentences.zh: 除湖北轉運判官，改提點湖北刑獄。

translations.literal: He was appointed vice commissioner of the Hubei transport circuit, then transferred to be judicial intendant for Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: He was made vice commissioner of the Hubei transport circuit and later reassigned as judicial intendant for Hubei.

sentences.zh: 岳飛宣撫荊湖，遇禼不以禮，禼憾之。

translations.literal: Yue Fei, as commissioner for Jinghu, treated Sijie without courtesy, and Sijie resented him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue Fei served as commissioner for the Jinghu region, he did not treat Sijie with proper respect, and Sijie bore a grudge.

sentences.zh: 禼入覲，調湖南轉運判官，陛辭，希秦檜意，譖飛於朝。

translations.literal: When Sijie came to court for an audience, he was reassigned as vice commissioner of the Hunan transport circuit. At his farewell audience he sought to please Qin Gui and slandered Yue Fei at court.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to court, Sijie was reassigned as vice commissioner of the Hunan transport circuit. At his farewell audience he curried favor with Qin Gui and denounced Yue Fei before the throne.

sentences.zh: 留為監察御史，擢右正言。

translations.literal: He was retained as investigating censor and promoted to right rectifier.
translations.idiomatic: He was kept at court as an investigating censor and soon promoted to right rectifier of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時檜謀收諸將兵權，禼力助之，言諸大將起行伍，知利不知義，畏死不畏法，高官大職，子女玉帛，已極其欲，盍示以逗遛之罰，敗亡之誅，不用命之戮，使知所懼。

translations.literal: At that time Gui plotted to recover military authority from the generals, and Sijie vigorously assisted him, saying that the great generals had risen from the ranks, knew profit but not righteousness, feared death but not the law, and with high office and great posts, sons and daughters, jade and silk, had already reached the limit of their desires—why not show them the penalty for delay, the punishment for defeat and ruin, and the execution for disobedience, so that they would know what to fear.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Gui was then scheming to strip the generals of their military authority, and Sijie strongly backed him. He argued that these commanders, raised from the ranks, knew gain but not duty, feared death but not the law, and with high rank, wealth, and families already had all they could want. He urged that they be shown penalties for delay, ruin, and disobedience so they would learn to fear the court.

sentences.zh: 張俊歸自楚州，與檜合謀擠飛，令禼劾飛對將佐言山陽不可守。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun returned from Chuzhou and joined Gui in a plot to squeeze out Yue Fei, ordering Sijie to impeach Fei for telling his officers and staff that Shanyang could not be held.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun returned from Chuzhou and conspired with Qin Gui to oust Yue Fei, directing Sijie to accuse Fei of telling his officers that Shanyang was indefensible.

sentences.zh: 命中丞何鑄治飛獄，鑄明其無辜。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Vice Censor-in-Chief He Zhu to try Fei's case, and Zhu established his innocence.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Vice Censor-in-Chief He Zhu to investigate the case, and Zhu found Yue Fei innocent.

sentences.zh: 檜怒，以禼代治，遂誣飛與其子雲致書張憲令虛申警報以動朝廷，及令憲措置使還飛軍；

translations.literal: Gui was enraged and had Sijie replace Zhu in the trial, then falsely charged that Fei and his son Yun had written to Zhang Xian ordering him to lodge false alarms to stir the court, and to arrange matters so that Fei's army would return;
translations.idiomatic: Qin Gui was furious and put Sijie in charge of the case instead. Sijie then fabricated charges that Yue Fei and his son Yun had written to Zhang Xian, urging him to raise false alarms to alarm the court and to arrange matters so Fei's troops would be recalled;

sentences.zh: 獄不成，又誣以淮西逗遛之事。

translations.literal: When the case would not stand, he further slandered him with the matter of delay on the Huai West campaign.
translations.idiomatic: When that case would not hold, he added the charge of deliberate delay during the Huai West campaign.

sentences.zh: 飛父子與憲俱死，天下冤之。

translations.literal: Fei, father and son, and Xian all died, and the realm regarded it as a grievous injustice.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei, his son Yun, and Zhang Xian were all put to death, and people throughout the empire considered it a gross injustice.

sentences.zh: 大理卿薛仁輔、寺丞李若朴、何彥猷言飛無罪，禼劾之；

translations.literal: Grand Court Judge Xue Renfu, court vice director Li Ruopu, and He Yanyou said Fei was innocent, and Sijie impeached them;
translations.idiomatic: Grand Court Judge Xue Renfu, Vice Director Li Ruopu, and He Yanyou declared Yue Fei innocent, and Sijie impeached them in turn;

sentences.zh: 知宗正寺士㒟請以百口保飛，禼又劾之，士㒟竄死建州。

translations.literal: Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan Shi Yun asked to guarantee Fei with the lives of a hundred family members, and Sijie again impeached him; Yun was banished and died in Jianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yun, director of the Court of the Imperial Clan, offered to stake the lives of his entire household on Yue Fei's innocence, but Sijie impeached him as well. Yun was exiled and died in Jianzhou.

sentences.zh: 劉洪道與飛有舊，禼劾其足恭媚飛，聞飛罷，宜撫抵掌流涕。

translations.literal: Liu Hongdao had old ties with Fei. Sijie impeached him for excessive deference and flattery toward Fei, and for clapping his hands and weeping when he heard that Fei had been dismissed as commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hongdao had long been close to Yue Fei. Sijie accused him of groveling before Fei and of clapping his hands and weeping when he learned that Fei had been removed as commissioner.

sentences.zh: 於是洪道抵罪，終身不復。

translations.literal: Thereupon Hongdao was convicted and never restored for the rest of his life.
translations.idiomatic: Hongdao was convicted on these charges and never held office again for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 參政範同為檜所引，或自奏事，檜忌之，禼劾罷，再論同罪，謫居筠州。

translations.literal: Participating Administrator Fan Tong had been brought in by Gui and sometimes memorialized on his own; Gui resented this, and Sijie impeached him and had him dismissed. Tong's offense was discussed again and he was demoted to live in Yunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Participating Administrator Fan Tong had been Qin Gui's protégé but sometimes submitted memorials on his own initiative, which Gui resented. Sijie impeached him and had him removed; when his case was reopened, he was banished to Yunzhou.

sentences.zh: 又為檜劾李光鼓倡，孫近朋比，二人皆被竄謫。

translations.literal: He also impeached at Gui's behest Li Guang for stirring agitation and Sun Jin for factional collusion; both men were banished.
translations.idiomatic: At Qin Gui's direction he also impeached Li Guang for inciting unrest and Sun Jin for forming a clique; both were exiled.

sentences.zh: 和議成，禼請詔戶部會計用兵之時與通和之後所費各幾何，若減於前日，乞以羨財別貯御前激賞庫，不許他用，蓄積稍實，可備緩急。

translations.literal: After the peace agreement was concluded, Sijie requested an edict ordering the Ministry of Revenue to calculate how much had been spent during the period of warfare and after peace was restored, and if the amount was less than before, to deposit the surplus separately in the imperial reward treasury before the throne, forbidding other use, so that accumulation might gradually become substantial and serve for emergencies.
translations.idiomatic: Once peace was concluded, Sijie asked that the Ministry of Revenue calculate wartime expenditures against post-peace costs. If spending had fallen, he proposed that the surplus be set aside in the imperial reward treasury, barred from other use, so reserves could build up for emergencies.

sentences.zh: 梓宮還，以禼為郐贊宮按行使，內侍省副都知宋唐卿副之，禼請與唐卿同班上殿奏事，其無恥如此。

translations.literal: When the late emperor's coffin returned, Sijie was made commissioner for the inspection mission accompanying the coffin to Kuai, with Song Tangqing, deputy director of the Inner Service Bureau, as his deputy. Sijie asked to ascend the hall and report affairs on the same schedule as Tangqing—his shamelessness was of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: When the late emperor's coffin was brought back, Sijie was appointed commissioner for the escort mission to Kuai, with Song Tangqing of the Inner Service Bureau as his deputy. He requested to share Tangqing's schedule for ascending the hall to report—such was his brazenness.

sentences.zh: 張浚寓居長沙，禼妄劾浚卜宅逾制，至擬五鳳樓。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun was living in retirement at Changsha. Sijie falsely impeached him for choosing a residence in excess of regulations, even comparing it to the Five Phoenix Tower.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun was living in retirement at Changsha when Sijie falsely accused him of building a residence that violated sumptuary regulations, comparing it even to the Five Phoenix Tower.

sentences.zh: 會吳秉信自長沙還朝，奏浚宅不過眾人，常產可辦，浚乃得免。

translations.literal: It happened that Wu Bingxin returned to court from Changsha and reported that Jun's residence was no more than what ordinary people had and could be afforded from normal property, and Jun was thus spared.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Bingxin happened to return from Changsha and reported that Jun's house was no grander than an ordinary man's and could be paid for from normal means, and Zhang Jun was spared.

sentences.zh: 除參知政事，充金國報謝使。

translations.literal: He was appointed participating administrator and served as envoy to the Jin state to return thanks.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed participating administrator and sent as envoy to the Jin court to return thanks.

sentences.zh: 使還，檜假金人譽己數千言，囑禼以聞，禼難之。

translations.literal: On his return from the mission, Gui forged several thousand words of Jin praise for himself and instructed Sijie to report them; Sijie found it difficult.
translations.idiomatic: After returning from his mission, he found that Qin Gui had fabricated several thousand words of Jin praise for himself and asked Sijie to report them to the throne. Sijie balked.

sentences.zh: 他日奏事退，檜坐殿廬中批上旨，輒除所厚者官，吏鈐紙尾進，禼曰：「不聞聖語。

translations.literal: Another day, after reporting on affairs and withdrawing, Gui sat in the side hall of the palace and drafted imperial rescripts, immediately appointing those he favored to office. When a clerk stamped the end of the paper and presented it, Sijie said, "I did not hear the sage's words.
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion, after court business Sijie withdrew while Qin Gui remained in the side hall drafting rescripts and immediately promoting his favorites. When a clerk brought the stamped document forward, Sijie said, "I did not hear the emperor's words.

sentences.zh: 」卻不視。

translations.literal: " and refused to look at it.
translations.idiomatic: He refused even to look at the document.

sentences.zh: 檜大怒，自是不交一語。

translations.literal: Gui was greatly enraged and from then on did not exchange a single word with him.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Gui was furious and thereafter would not speak a word to him.

sentences.zh: 言官李文會、詹大方交章劾禼，禼遂求去。

translations.literal: Censorial officials Li Wenhui and Zhan Dafang submitted successive memorials impeaching Sijie, and Sijie then requested to leave office.
translations.idiomatic: Censorial officials Li Wenhui and Zhan Dafang filed successive impeachments against him, and Sijie asked to resign.

sentences.zh: 帝命出守，檜愈怒。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered him to go out as prefect, and Gui grew still angrier.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered him to take a prefectural post outside the capital, which only deepened Qin Gui's anger.

sentences.zh: 給事中楊願封還詞頭，遂罷去，尋謫居歸州。

translations.literal: Drafting drafter Yang Yuan returned the appointment text sealed shut, and Sijie was then dismissed; soon he was demoted to live in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Drafting drafter Yang Yuan returned the appointment edict unapproved, and Sijie was dismissed. He was soon banished to Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 遇赦，量移沅州。

translations.literal: He encountered an amnesty and was transferred under discretion to Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After an amnesty he was transferred under discretion to Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，召還，除參知政事，尋拜尚書右僕射、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was recalled, appointed participating administrator, and soon invested as right vice director of the Department of State Affairs and concurrent Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year of Shaoxing he was recalled, made participating administrator, and soon promoted to right vice director of the Department of State Affairs and Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 纂次太后回鑾事實，上之。

translations.literal: He compiled the factual record of the empress dowager's return journey and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled a factual account of the empress dowager's return to the capital and submitted it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 張浚以禼與沈該居相位不厭天下望，上書言其專欲受命于金。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun, because Sijie and Shen Gai held the chancellorship to the dissatisfaction of public expectation, submitted a memorial saying that they wished exclusively to receive their mandate from the Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun, believing that Sijie and Shen Gai in office failed to meet public expectations, memorialized that they sought only to take their orders from the Jin.

sentences.zh: 禼見書大怒，以為金人未有釁，而浚所奏乃若禍在年歲間，浚坐竄謫。

translations.literal: Sijie, on seeing the memorial, was greatly enraged, thinking that the Jin had given no cause for offense while Jun's memorial made it seem as though disaster were only years away; Jun was banished on this account.
translations.idiomatic: Sijie was furious when he read it, arguing that the Jin had given no provocation while Jun's memorial made war sound imminent. Zhang Jun was exiled as a result.

sentences.zh: 禼提舉刊修《貢舉敕令格式》五十卷、《看詳法意》四百八十七卷，書進，授金紫光祿大夫，致仕。

translations.literal: Sijie supervised the compilation and revision of fifty juan of Examination Decrees, Regulations, and Formats and four hundred eighty-seven juan of Reviewed Legal Intent; when the books were presented he was granted the golden purple-girdle grand master of splendid happiness and retired.
translations.idiomatic: He supervised compilation of fifty juan of examination statutes and four hundred eighty-seven juan of reviewed legal commentary. When the works were submitted he was granted the golden purple-girdle grand master rank and retired from office.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十五，諡忠靖。

translations.literal: He died at the age of seventy-five, and was given the posthumous title Zhongjing.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-five and was posthumously titled Loyal and Tranquil.

sentences.zh: 禼始附檜，為言官，所言多出檜意；

translations.literal: Sijie at first attached himself to Gui as a censorial official, and what he said mostly came from Gui's intent;
translations.idiomatic: Sijie had first attached himself to Qin Gui as a censorial official, and his pronouncements largely echoed Gui's wishes;

sentences.zh: 及登政府，不能受鉗制，遂忤檜去。

translations.literal: when he entered the government he could not accept being controlled and thus offended Gui and left.
translations.idiomatic: but once he reached high office he would not submit to Gui's control, offended him, and was driven out.

sentences.zh: 檜死，帝親政，將反檜所為，首召禼還。

translations.literal: When Gui died the emperor took personal rule and intended to reverse what Gui had done, first recalling Sijie.
translations.idiomatic: After Qin Gui's death the emperor took personal control and planned to undo his policies, recalling Sijie first among the exiles.

sentences.zh: 禼主和固位，無異於檜，士論益薄之。

translations.literal: Sijie upheld peace to secure his position, no different from Gui, and scholarly opinion despised him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Sijie upheld peace to keep his position, no differently from Qin Gui, and educated opinion despised him all the more.

sentences.zh: 韓侂胄

translations.literal: Han Tuozhou
translations.idiomatic: Han Tuozhou

sentences.zh: 韓侂胄位元組夫，魏忠獻王琦曾孫也。

translations.literal: Han Tuozhou was a son-in-law of the emperor by rank, a great-great-grandson of Prince Zhongxian of Wei, Han Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Han Tuozhou was an imperial son-in-law by rank and a great-great-grandson of Han Qi, Prince Zhongxian of Wei.

sentences.zh: 父誠，娶高宗憲聖慈烈皇后女弟，仕至寶甯軍承宣使。

translations.literal: His father Cheng married a younger sister of Empress Dowager Xiansheng Cilie, consort of Emperor Gaozong, and rose to commissioner of the Baoning Army.
translations.idiomatic: His father Cheng married a younger sister of Empress Dowager Xiansheng Cilie of Gaozong and rose to commissioner of the Baoning Army.

sentences.zh: 侂胄以父任入官，曆閣門祗候、宣贊舍人、帶禦器械。

translations.literal: Tuozhou entered office through his father's privilege, and successively served as gate attendant of the Privy Portal, palace announcer, and bearer of the imperial armory insignia.
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou entered office through his father's privilege and served in turn as gate attendant of the Privy Portal, palace announcer, and bearer of the imperial armory insignia.

sentences.zh: 淳熙末，以汝州防禦使知閣門事。

translations.literal: At the end of the Chunxi reign he served as defender of Ruzhou while directing affairs of the Privy Portal.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Chunxi era he served as defender of Ruzhou while directing affairs of the Privy Portal.

sentences.zh: 孝宗崩，光宗以疾不能執喪，中外洶洶，趙汝愚議定策立皇子嘉王。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozong died, Emperor Guangzong was ill and unable to preside over mourning; inside and outside the court were in uproar, and Zhao Ruyu proposed settling the succession by enthroning the prince, Prince Jia.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozong died, Emperor Guangzong was too ill to preside over the mourning rites, and court and country were in turmoil. Zhao Ruyu proposed enthroning the prince, Prince Jia.

sentences.zh: 時憲聖太后居慈福宮，而侂胄雅善慈福內侍張宗尹，汝愚乃使侂胄介宗尹以其議密啟太后。

translations.literal: At that time Empress Dowager Xiansheng resided in Cifu Palace, and Tuozhou was on good terms with the Cifu inner attendant Zhang Zongyin; Ruyu therefore had Tuozhou go through Zongyin to report their plan secretly to the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Xiansheng was then at Cifu Palace, and Tuozhou was on good terms with her attendant Zhang Zongyin. Ruyu had Tuozhou convey their plan to the empress dowager through Zongyin in secret.

sentences.zh: 侂胄兩至宮門，不獲命，彷徨欲退，遇重華宮提舉關禮問故，入白憲聖，言甚懇切，憲聖可其議。

translations.literal: Tuozhou twice came to the palace gate but received no command, hesitated and was about to withdraw, when he met Guan Li, superintendent of Chonghua Palace, who asked his reason; Li entered and reported to Xiansheng, speaking with great earnestness, and Xiansheng approved the plan.
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou came twice to the palace gate but received no answer and was about to withdraw in dismay when Guan Li, superintendent of Chonghua Palace, asked his business. Li went in, reported earnestly to the empress dowager, and she approved the plan.

sentences.zh: 禮以告侂胄，侂胄馳白汝愚。

translations.literal: Li told Tuozhou, and Tuozhou galloped to inform Ruyu.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Li told Tuozhou, who galloped off to inform Zhao Ruyu.

sentences.zh: 日已向夕，汝愚亟命殿帥郭杲以所部兵夜分衛南北內。

translations.literal: The day was already toward evening; Ruyu urgently ordered Palace Commander Guo Gao to use his troops at midnight to guard the inner and outer palaces north and south.
translations.idiomatic: Evening was falling when Ruyu urgently ordered Palace Commander Guo Gao to deploy his troops at midnight to guard the inner and outer palaces.

sentences.zh: 翌日，憲聖太后即喪次垂簾，宰臣傳旨，命嘉王即皇帝位。

translations.literal: The next day Empress Dowager Xiansheng drew the curtain at the mourning site, the chief ministers transmitted the edict, and ordered Prince Jia to ascend the imperial throne.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Empress Dowager Xiansheng drew the curtain at the mourning hall, the chief ministers transmitted her edict, and Prince Jia was enthroned as emperor.

sentences.zh: 甯宗既立，侂胄欲推定策恩，汝愚曰：「吾宗臣也，汝外戚也，何可以言功？

translations.literal: After Emperor Ningzong was established, Tuozhou wished to claim merit for settling the succession. Ruyu said, "I am a clansman of the imperial house and you are an affinal relative—how can you speak of merit?
translations.idiomatic: Once Emperor Ningzong was enthroned, Tuozhou sought reward for helping settle the succession. Zhao Ruyu said, "I am a clansman of the house and you are an affinal relative—how can either of us claim merit?

sentences.zh: 惟爪牙之臣，則當推賞。

translations.literal: Only the henchmen should receive promotion and reward.
translations.idiomatic: Only the men who carried it out deserve reward.

sentences.zh: 」乃加郭杲節鉞，而侂胄但遷宜州觀察使兼樞密都承旨。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Guo Gao was given a military commission, while Tuozhou was only transferred to observer of Yizhou and concurrent chief coordinator of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: " Guo Gao was given a military commission, while Tuozhou was merely promoted to observer of Yizhou and chief coordinator of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 侂胄始觖望，然以傳導詔旨，浸見親幸，時時乘間竊弄威福。

translations.literal: Tuozhou was at first discontent, but because he transmitted imperial edicts he gradually came to be favored, and from time to time seized opportunities to wield authority and bestow favors in secret.
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou was resentful at first, but because he relayed imperial edicts he gradually won favor and began to seize chances to wield power and grant favors on his own.

sentences.zh: 朱熹白汝愚當用厚賞酬其勞而疏遠之，汝愚不以為意。

translations.literal: Zhu Xi told Ruyu that he should use generous reward to repay Tuozhou's labor but keep him at a distance; Ruyu paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xi advised Ruyu to reward Tuozhou generously but keep him at arm's length. Ruyu ignored the advice.

sentences.zh: 右正言黃度欲劾侂胄，謀泄，斥去。

translations.literal: Right rectifier Huang Du wished to impeach Tuozhou; the plot leaked and he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Right rectifier Huang Du planned to impeach Tuozhou, but the plot leaked and Huang was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 朱熹奏其奸，侂胄怒，使優人峨冠闊袖象大儒，戲于上前，熹遂去。

translations.literal: Zhu Xi memorialized about his wickedness; Tuozhou was enraged and had actors wear high caps and broad sleeves to imitate great Confucians and perform before the emperor; Xi then left office.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xi memorialized against his misconduct. Tuozhou was furious and had actors dress as great Confucian scholars to mock Xi before the throne, and Zhu Xi left office.

sentences.zh: 彭龜年請留熹而逐侂胄。

translations.literal: Peng Guinian asked to retain Xi and expel Tuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Guinian asked that Zhu Xi be kept and Tuozhou expelled.

sentences.zh: 未幾，龜年與郡；

translations.literal: Before long, Guinian was given a prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: Before long Peng Guinian was sent out to a prefecture;

sentences.zh: 侂胄進保甯軍承宣使，提舉佑神觀。

translations.literal: Tuozhou was advanced to commissioner of the Baoning Army and made superintendent of the You Shen Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou was promoted to commissioner of the Baoning Army and made superintendent of the You Shen Abbey.

sentences.zh: 自是，胄益用事，而以抑賞故，怨汝愚日深。

translations.literal: From this time Tuozhou wielded power all the more, and because his rewards had been held back he resented Ruyu ever more deeply day by day.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Tuozhou wielded greater power, and because his rewards had been curtailed his resentment of Zhao Ruyu deepened daily.

sentences.zh: 縗川劉弼者，曩與侂胄同知閣門事，頗以知書自負。

translations.literal: Liu Bi of Cuichuan had formerly served with Tuozhou as co-director of the Privy Portal and prided himself considerably on his learning.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bi of Cuichuan had once served with Tuozhou as co-director of the Privy Portal and prided himself on his learning.

sentences.zh: 方議內禪時，汝愚獨與侂胄計議，弼弗得與聞，內懷不平，至是，謂侂胄曰：「趙相欲專大功，君豈惟不得節度，將恐不免嶺海之行矣。

translations.literal: When the inner abdication was being discussed, Ruyu deliberated only with Tuozhou and Bi was not allowed to hear of it; he harbored resentment within. By this time he said to Tuozhou, "Chancellor Zhao wishes to monopolize the great merit—will you not only fail to receive a military commission, you may well not escape banishment to the Lingnan seas.
translations.idiomatic: When the inner abdication was being planned, Zhao Ruyu consulted only Tuozhou and excluded Bi, who nursed a grievance. He now told Tuozhou, "Chancellor Zhao means to keep all the credit for himself. You will not only miss out on a military commission—you may well be banished to the far south.

sentences.zh: 」侂胄愕然，因問計，弼曰：「惟有用台諫爾。

translations.literal: " Tuozhou was startled and asked his plan; Bi said, "There is only the use of the censorial and remonstrance officials.
translations.idiomatic: " Tuozhou was alarmed and asked what to do. Bi said, "You must use the censorial and remonstrance officials.

sentences.zh: 」侂胄問：「若何而可？

translations.literal: " Tuozhou asked, "How can that be done?
translations.idiomatic: " Tuozhou asked, "How can that be done?

sentences.zh: 」弼曰：「御筆批出是也。

translations.literal: " Bi said, "An imperial brush rescript is what is needed.
translations.idiomatic: " Bi said, "Issue appointments by imperial brush rescript."

sentences.zh: 」侂胄悟，即以內批除所知劉德秀為監察御史，楊大法為殿中侍御史；

translations.literal: " Tuozhou understood, and immediately by inner rescript appointed his acquaintance Liu Dexiu as investigating censor and Yang Dafa as palace censor;
translations.idiomatic: " Tuozhou understood at once. By inner rescript he appointed his ally Liu Dexiu investigating censor and Yang Dafa palace censor;

sentences.zh: 罷吳獵監察御史，而用劉三傑代之。

translations.literal: he dismissed Wu Lie as investigating censor and replaced him with Liu Sanjie.
translations.idiomatic: dismissed Wu Lie as investigating censor and replaced him with Liu Sanjie.

sentences.zh: 於是言路皆侂胄之黨，汝愚之跡始危。

translations.literal: Thereupon the remonstrance route was entirely Tuozhou's faction, and Ruyu's position began to be perilous.
translations.idiomatic: The remonstrance route was now entirely Tuozhou's faction, and Zhao Ruyu's position began to look precarious.

sentences.zh: 侂胄欲逐汝愚而難其名，謀於京鏜，鏜曰：「彼宗姓，誣以謀危社稷可也。

translations.literal: Tuozhou wished to expel Ruyu but found it hard to name a charge; he consulted Jing Tang, who said, "He is of the imperial clan—slander him with plotting to endanger the altars of state and that will do.
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou wanted to oust Zhao Ruyu but lacked a charge. He consulted Jing Tang, who said, "He is of the imperial clan—accuse him of plotting against the state."

sentences.zh: 」慶元元年，侂胄引李沐為右正言。

translations.literal: " In the first year of Qingyuan, Tuozhou brought in Li Mu as right rectifier.
translations.idiomatic: " In the first year of Qingyuan (1195), Tuozhou installed Li Mu as right rectifier.

sentences.zh: 沐嘗有求於汝愚不獲，即奏汝愚以同姓居相位，將不利於社稷。

translations.literal: Mu had once made a request of Ruyu and not obtained it; he immediately memorialized that Ruyu, as one of the same surname holding the chancellorship, would be harmful to the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mu had once asked a favor of Zhao Ruyu and been refused. He now memorialized that Ruyu, as a clansman holding the chancellorship, would endanger the state.

sentences.zh: 汝愚罷相。

translations.literal: Ruyu was dismissed from the chancellorship.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ruyu was dismissed from the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 始，侂胄之見汝愚，徐誼實薦之，汝愚既斥，遂並逐誼。

translations.literal: At the beginning, when Tuozhou had been introduced to Ruyu, it was Xu Yi who had actually recommended him; after Ruyu was expelled, Yi was also driven out.
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou had originally been introduced to Zhao Ruyu by Xu Yi. When Ruyu fell, Yi was expelled as well.

sentences.zh: 朱熹、彭龜年、黃度、李祥、楊簡、呂祖儉等以攻侂胄得罪，太學生楊宏中、張衙、徐范、蔣傅、林仲麟、周端朝等又以上書論侂胄編置，朝士以言侂胄遭責者數十人。

translations.literal: Zhu Xi, Peng Guinian, Huang Du, Li Xiang, Yang Jian, Lü Zujian, and others offended through attacking Tuozhou; Imperial University students Yang Hongzhong, Zhang Ya, Xu Fan, Jiang Fu, Lin Zhonglin, Zhou Duanchao, and others again submitted memorials discussing Tuozhou and were banished; court officials who spoke against Tuozhou and were punished numbered several tens.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xi, Peng Guinian, Huang Du, Li Xiang, Yang Jian, Lü Zujian, and others were punished for attacking Tuozhou. Imperial University students Yang Hongzhong, Zhang Ya, Xu Fan, Jiang Fu, Lin Zhonglin, and Zhou Duanchao memorialized against him and were banished. Dozens of court officials who spoke out against Tuozhou were punished.

sentences.zh: 已而侂胄拜保甯軍節度使、提舉佑神觀。

translations.literal: Before long Tuozhou was invested as military commissioner of the Baoning Army and superintendent of the You Shen Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Tuozhou was made military commissioner of the Baoning Army and superintendent of the You Shen Abbey.

sentences.zh: 又設偽學之目，以網括汝愚、朱熹門下知名之士。

translations.literal: He also established the category of "false learning" to net the renowned men under Ruyu and Zhu Xi.
translations.idiomatic: He also created the label of "false learning" to ensnare prominent followers of Zhao Ruyu and Zhu Xi.

sentences.zh: 用何澹、胡鲶為言官。

translations.literal: He employed He Dan and Hu Nian as censorial officials.
translations.idiomatic: He installed He Dan and Hu Nian as censorial officials.

sentences.zh: 澹言偽學宜加風厲，或指汝愚為偽學罪首。

translations.literal: Dan said false learning should be subjected to stern admonition, and some pointed to Ruyu as the chief culprit of false learning.
translations.idiomatic: He Dan urged stern measures against false learning, and some named Zhao Ruyu as its ringleader.

sentences.zh: 鲶條奏汝愚有十不遜，且及徐誼。

translations.literal: Nian submitted a detailed memorial that Ruyu had ten instances of insubordination, and implicated Xu Yi as well.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Nian submitted a detailed memorial listing ten acts of insubordination by Zhao Ruyu and implicating Xu Yi as well.

sentences.zh: 汝愚謫永州，誼謫南安軍。

translations.literal: Ruyu was demoted to Yongzhou and Yi to Nan'an Army.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ruyu was banished to Yongzhou and Xu Yi to Nan'an Army.

sentences.zh: 慮他日汝愚復用，密諭衡守錢鍪圖之，汝愚抵衡暴薨。

translations.literal: Fearing that Ruyu might one day be employed again, he secretly instructed Hengzhou prefect Qian Mou to plot against him; when Ruyu reached Heng he suddenly died.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Zhao Ruyu might one day return to power, Tuozhou secretly instructed Hengzhou prefect Qian Mou to deal with him. Ruyu died suddenly on reaching Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 留正舊在都堂眾辱侂胄，至是，劉德秀論正引用偽黨，正坐罷斥。

translations.literal: Liu Zheng had formerly humiliated Tuozhou before the whole hall at the capital; by this time Liu Dexiu argued that Zheng employed the false-learning faction, and Zheng was dismissed on this charge.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zheng had once humiliated Tuozhou openly in the chief ministers' hall. Liu Dexiu now accused him of employing the false-learning faction, and Zheng was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書葉翥要侍郎倪思列疏論偽學，思不從，侂胄乃擢翥執政而免思官。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Ye He wanted Vice Director Ni Si to submit a joint memorial on false learning; Si refused, and Tuozhou then promoted He to the government and stripped Si of office.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Ye He wanted Vice Director Ni Si to join a memorial against false learning. When Si refused, Tuozhou promoted Ye to high office and stripped Si of his post.

sentences.zh: 侂胄加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Tuozhou was given the additional title of commissioner with credentials equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou was granted the honorary title of commissioner with credentials equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 時台諫迎合侂胄意，以攻偽學為言，然憚清議，不欲顯斥熹。

translations.literal: At that time the censorial and remonstrance officials catered to Tuozhou's intent and spoke of attacking false learning, yet they feared pure opinion and did not wish openly to expel Xi.
translations.idiomatic: The censorial and remonstrance officials now echoed Tuozhou and attacked false learning, yet they feared public opinion and hesitated to denounce Zhu Xi openly.

sentences.zh: 侂胄意未快，以陳賈嘗攻熹，召除賈兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: Tuozhou was not yet satisfied and, because Chen Jia had once attacked Xi, summoned and appointed Jia vice director of the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou was still unsatisfied. Because Chen Jia had once attacked Zhu Xi, he summoned Chen and appointed him vice director of the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 未至，亟除沈繼祖台察。

translations.literal: Before Jia arrived, he urgently appointed Shen Jizu as censorial investigator.
translations.idiomatic: Before Chen could take up the post, he urgently appointed Shen Jizu censorial investigator.

sentences.zh: 繼祖誣熹十罪，落職罷祠。

translations.literal: Jizu falsely charged Xi with ten crimes, and Xi was stripped of office and deprived of his sacrificial stipend.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Jizu fabricated ten charges against Zhu Xi, who was stripped of office and deprived of his sacrificial stipend.

sentences.zh: 三年，劉三傑入對，言前日偽黨，今變而為逆黨。

translations.literal: In the third year Liu Sanjie entered for audience and said that the former false-learning faction had now turned into a faction of treason.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Liu Sanjie appeared before the throne and declared that the former false-learning faction had now become a treasonous faction.

sentences.zh: 侂胄大喜，即日除三傑為右正言，而坐偽學逆黨得罪者五十有九人。

translations.literal: Tuozhou was greatly pleased and that same day appointed Sanjie right rectifier; those convicted on the charge of false learning and treasonous faction numbered fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou was delighted and that same day made Sanjie right rectifier. Fifty-nine men were punished as members of the false-learning treasonous faction.

sentences.zh: 王沇獻言令省部籍記偽學姓名，姚愈請降詔嚴偽學之禁，二人皆得遷官。

translations.literal: Wang Yi proposed that the ministries and departments register the names of false-learning adherents; Yao Yu asked that an edict be issued to tighten the ban on false learning; both men were promoted.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yi proposed that ministries register the names of false-learning adherents, and Yao Yu asked for an edict tightening the ban. Both were promoted.

sentences.zh: 施康年、陳讜、鄧友龍、林采皆以攻偽學久居言路，而張釜、張岩、程松率由此秉政。

translations.literal: Shi Kangnian, Chen Dan, Deng Youlong, and Lin Cai all long held the remonstrance route through attacking false learning, while Zhang Fu, Zhang Yan, and Cheng Song for the most part came to wield government power by this path.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Kangnian, Chen Dan, Deng Youlong, and Lin Cai long held censorial posts through attacking false learning, while Zhang Fu, Zhang Yan, and Cheng Song largely rose to power by the same route.

sentences.zh: 四年，侂胄拜少傅，封豫國公。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Tuozhou was appointed Junior Tutor and enfeoffed as Duke of Yu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, Han Tuozhou was appointed Junior Tutor and enfeoffed as Duke of Yu.

sentences.zh: 有蔡璉者嘗得罪，汝愚執而黥之。

translations.literal: There was one Cai Lian who had once offended; Ruyu arrested him and tattooed him.
translations.idiomatic: A man named Cai Lian had once offended Zhao Ruyu, who had him arrested and branded.

sentences.zh: 五年，侂胄使璉告汝愚定策時有異謀，具其賓客所言七十紙。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Tuozhou had Lian accuse Ruyu of harboring a different plot at the time of setting the succession, providing seventy sheets of what his guests had said.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, Han Tuozhou had Cai Lian accuse Zhao Ruyu of treacherous designs during the succession crisis, submitting seventy pages of statements by Ruyu's retainers.

sentences.zh: 侂胄欲逮彭龜年、曾三聘、徐誼、沈有開下大理鞫之，范仲藝力爭乃止。

translations.literal: Tuozhou wished to arrest Peng Guinian, Zeng Sanpin, Xu Yi, and Shen Youkai and send them down to the Court of Judicial Review for interrogation; Fan Zhongyi argued forcefully and it was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou wanted to arrest Peng Guinian, Zeng Sanpin, Xu Yi, and Shen Youkai and interrogate them in the Court of Judicial Review, but Fan Zhongyi protested vigorously and the plan was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 其年遷少師，封平原郡王。

translations.literal: That year he was transferred to Junior Preceptor and enfeoffed as Prince of Pingyuan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he was promoted to Junior Preceptor and enfeoffed as Prince of Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 六年，進太傅。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he was advanced to Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, he was promoted to Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 婺州布衣呂祖泰上書言道學不可禁，請誅侂胄，以周必大為相。

translations.literal: A commoner of Wuzhou, Lü Zutai, submitted a memorial saying the Way-learning could not be banned, asking that Tuozhou be executed and Zhou Bida made chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Zutai, a commoner from Wuzhou, submitted a memorial arguing that the Way-learning must not be suppressed. He called for Tuozhou's execution and for Zhou Bida to be made chief minister.

sentences.zh: 侂胄大怒，決杖流欽州。

translations.literal: Tuozhou was greatly enraged and had him beaten with the cudgel and exiled to Qin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou was furious and had him beaten and exiled to Qin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 言者希侂胄意，劾必大首植偽黨。

translations.literal: Memorialists conformed to Tuozhou's intent and impeached Bida as the chief planter of the false-learning faction.
translations.idiomatic: Memorialists seeking to please Tuozhou impeached Zhou Bida as the ringleader of the false-learning faction.

sentences.zh: 降為少保。

translations.literal: He was demoted to Junior Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: Bida was demoted to Junior Guardian.

sentences.zh: 一時善類悉罹黨禍，雖本侂胄意，而謀實始京鏜。

translations.literal: For a time all good men suffered factional calamity; although it originated in Tuozhou's intent, the plot in fact began with Jing Zong.
translations.idiomatic: Many good men of the day fell victim to the factional purge. Though it served Tuozhou's designs, the scheme had actually originated with Jing Zong.

sentences.zh: 逮鏜死，侂胄亦稍厭前事，張孝伯以為不弛黨禁，後恐不免報復之禍。

translations.literal: When Zong died, Tuozhou also slightly wearied of previous matters; Zhang Xiaobo held that if the faction ban were not relaxed, afterward one might not escape retribution.
translations.idiomatic: After Jing Zong died, Tuozhou too began to tire of the persecution. Zhang Xiaobo warned that if the faction ban was not lifted, retribution would surely follow.

sentences.zh: 侂胄以為然，追復汝愚、朱熹職名，留正、周必大亦復秩還政，徐誼等皆先後復官。

translations.literal: Tuozhou thought this correct and posthumously restored Ruyu and Xi's official titles; Liu Zheng and Zhou Bida also had rank restored and returned to government, and Xu Yi and others all in turn had offices restored.
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou agreed. He posthumously restored the official titles of Zhao Ruyu and Zhu Xi, reinstated Liu Zheng and Zhou Bida to office, and gradually restored Xu Yi and others to their posts.

sentences.zh: 偽党之禁浸解。

translations.literal: The ban on the false faction gradually relaxed.
translations.idiomatic: The ban on the false-learning faction was gradually eased.

sentences.zh: 三年，拜太師。

translations.literal: In the third year, he was appointed Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, he was appointed Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 監惠民局夏允中上書，請侂胄平章國政，侂胄繆為辭謝，乞致其仕，詔不許，允中放罷。

translations.literal: Supervisor of the Bureau for Public Benefit Xia Yunzhong submitted a memorial asking that Tuozhou jointly govern the state; Tuozhou falsely declined and begged to retire, an edict did not permit it, and Yunzhong was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Yunzhong, supervisor of the Bureau for Public Benefit, submitted a memorial asking that Tuozhou jointly administer state affairs. Tuozhou feigned refusal and asked to retire, but the emperor would not allow it; Yunzhong was dismissed instead.

sentences.zh: 時侂胄以勢利蠱士大夫之心，薛叔似、辛棄疾、陳謙皆起廢顯用，當時固有困於久斥，損晚節以規榮進者矣。

translations.literal: At that time Tuozhou by power and profit bewitched the minds of scholar-officials; Xue Shushi, Xin Qiji, and Chen Qian were all raised from dismissal to conspicuous employment; at the time there truly were those trapped by long dismissal who damaged their late years seeking advancement through glory.
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou now used power and patronage to sway the scholar-official class. Xue Shushi, Xin Qiji, and Chen Qian were all recalled from disgrace to high office. Some, worn down by long exile, compromised their reputations in hopes of advancement.

sentences.zh: 若陳自強則以侂胄童子師，自選人不數年致位宰相，而蘇師旦、周筠又侂胄廝役也，亦皆預聞國政，超取顯仕。

translations.literal: As for Chen Ziqiang, he was Tuozhou's tutor when a youth and from candidate rose to chief minister within not a few years; while Su Shidan and Zhou Yun were also Tuozhou's servile attendants, and all alike participated in hearing state affairs and leaped to conspicuous office.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Ziqiang had been Tuozhou's childhood tutor and rose from a lowly candidate to chief minister within a few years. Su Shidan and Zhou Yun, former servants in Tuozhou's household, also gained access to state affairs and vaulted to high office.

sentences.zh: 群小阿附，勢焰熏灼。

translations.literal: The multitude of petty men fawned and attached themselves, their power and flame scorching bright.
translations.idiomatic: A host of petty men flocked to his side, their influence blazing unchecked.

sentences.zh: 侂胄凡所欲為，宰執惕息不敢為異，自強至印空名敕劄授之，惟所欲用，三省不預知也。

translations.literal: Whatever Tuozhou wished to do, the chief ministers trembled and dared not differ; from Ziqiang down they merely stamped empty-name edict slips and handed them over, using whomever he wished—the Three Departments were not forewarned.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever Tuozhou wished, the chief ministers trembled and dared not dissent. Chen Ziqiang and the others merely stamped pre-signed edicts and handed them over, appointing whomever Tuozhou chose without consulting the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 言路厄塞，每月舉論二三常事而已，謂之月課。

translations.literal: The remonstrance route was blocked and constricted; each month only two or three routine matters were raised for discussion—that was called the monthly assignment.
translations.idiomatic: The channels of remonstrance were choked off. Censors discussed only two or three routine matters each month in what was called the monthly assignment.

sentences.zh: 或勸侂胄立蓋世功名以自固者，於是恢復之議興。

translations.literal: Some advised Tuozhou to establish epoch-making merit to secure himself, and thus the discussion of recovery arose.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged Tuozhou to secure his position with a towering military achievement, and talk of recovering the Central Plains began.

sentences.zh: 以殿前都指揮使吳曦為興州都統，識者多言曦不可，主西師必叛，侂胄不省。

translations.literal: He made Commander-in-Chief of the Palace Front Wu Xi commander of Xing Prefecture; those in the know mostly said Xi should not be used, and that placing him in charge of western troops he would surely rebel—Tuozhou did not perceive this.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Wu Xi, commander-in-chief of the Palace Front, as military commissioner of Xing Prefecture. Observers warned that Xi would rebel if given command of western forces, but Tuozhou paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 安豐守厲仲方言淮北流民願歸附，會辛棄疾入見，言敵國必亂必亡，願屬元老大臣預為應變計，鄭挺、鄧友龍等又附和其言。

translations.literal: Prefect of Anfeng Li Zhongfang said that refugees north of the Huai wished to submit; it happened that Xin Qiji entered for audience and said the enemy state would surely fall into disorder and perish, wishing that veteran great ministers be entrusted to prepare contingency plans; Zheng Ting, Deng Youlong, and others also echoed his words.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect of Anfeng Li Zhongfang reported that refugees north of the Huai wished to return to Song rule. Xin Qiji, appearing before the throne, declared the Jurchen regime was doomed and urged senior ministers to prepare for the opportunity. Zheng Ting, Deng Youlong, and others seconded him.

sentences.zh: 開禧改元，進士毛自知廷對，言當乘機以定中原，侂胄大悅。

translations.literal: When the reign era changed to Kaixi, presented scholar Mao Zizhi answered at court audience and said one should seize the opportunity to settle the Central Plains—Tuozhou was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When the reign title was changed to Kaixi, Mao Zizhi, a presented scholar, answered at court audience that the moment had come to retake the Central Plains. Tuozhou was delighted.

sentences.zh: 詔中外諸將密為行軍之計。

translations.literal: An edict ordered generals inside and outside secretly to make military march plans.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered generals throughout the empire to prepare war plans in secret.

sentences.zh: 先是，楊輔、傅伯成言兵不可動，抵罪。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yang Fu and Fu Bocheng had said troops must not be moved and were punished.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Yang Fu and Fu Bocheng had warned against mobilization and were punished for it.

sentences.zh: 至是，武學生華岳叩閽乞斬侂胄、蘇師旦、周筠以謝天下，諫議大夫李大異亦論止開邊。

translations.literal: By this time Military Academy student Hua Yue beat the palace gate begging to behead Tuozhou, Su Shidan, and Zhou Yun to answer to the realm; Remonstrance and Discussion Grandee Li Dayi also argued to stop opening the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Now Hua Yue, a student of the Military Academy, beat the palace gate demanding that Tuozhou, Su Shidan, and Zhou Yun be executed to appease the nation. Remonstrance Grandee Li Dayi also urged halting the frontier war.

sentences.zh: 嶽下大理劾罪編置，大異斥去。

translations.literal: Yue was sent down to the Court of Judicial Review, charged with crimes and registered for exile; Dayi was expelled.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Yue was tried by the Court of Judicial Review and exiled. Li Dayi was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 陳自強援故事乞命侂胄兼領平章，台諫鄧友龍等繼以為請，侂胄除平章軍國事。

translations.literal: Chen Ziqiang cited precedent and begged that Tuozhou be ordered concurrently to head the Secretariat-Chancellery; censorial remonstrators Deng Youlong and others followed with the same request; Tuozhou was appointed director of military and state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Ziqiang cited precedent and requested that Tuozhou be granted concurrent authority over military and civil affairs. Censors including Deng Youlong joined the plea, and Tuozhou was appointed director of military and state affairs.

sentences.zh: 蕭逵、李壁時在太常，論定典禮，三日一朝，因至都堂，序班丞相之上，三省印並納其第。

translations.literal: Xiao Kui and Li Bi were then in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and settled the ritual regulations: an audience every three days, and when he came to the chief ministers' hall he ranked above the chief ministers; the seals of the Three Departments were all deposited at his residence.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Kui and Li Bi of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices set the ritual protocol: Tuozhou would attend court every three days, take precedence over the chief ministers when he entered the hall, and keep the seals of the Three Departments at his residence.

sentences.zh: 侂胄昵蘇師旦為腹心，除師旦安遠軍節度使。

translations.literal: Tuozhou was intimate with Su Shidan as his trusted inner circle and appointed Shidan military commissioner of Anyuan Army.
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou treated Su Shidan as his closest confidant and appointed him military commissioner of Anyuan.

sentences.zh: 自置機速房於私第，甚者假作御筆，升黜將帥，事關機要，未嘗奏稟，人莫敢言。

translations.literal: He himself set up a Rapid Affairs Office at his private residence; in extreme cases he forged the emperor's brush, promoting and demoting generals; matters touching on vital secrets were never submitted for approval, and no one dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: He established a Rapid Affairs Office in his private residence. He even forged imperial edicts to promote and demote generals. Matters of critical import were never reported to the throne, and no one dared protest.

sentences.zh: 二年，以薛叔似為京湖宣諭使；

translations.literal: In the second year, Xue Shushi was made commissioner to proclaim and reassure in Jing-Hu;
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, Xue Shushi was appointed commissioner to proclaim and reassure in the Jing-Hu circuit;

sentences.zh: 鄧友龍為兩淮宣諭使；

translations.literal: Deng Youlong was made commissioner to proclaim and reassure in the Two Huai;
translations.idiomatic: Deng Youlong was appointed commissioner in the Two Huai circuit;

sentences.zh: 程松為四川宣撫使，吳曦副之。

translations.literal: Cheng Song was made pacification commissioner of Sichuan, with Wu Xi as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Song was appointed Sichuan pacification commissioner, with Wu Xi as deputy.

sentences.zh: 徐邦憲自處州召見，以弭兵為言，忤侂胄意，削二秩。

translations.literal: Xu Bangxian was summoned from Chuzhou for audience; speaking of halting troops, he offended Tuozhou's intent and was stripped of two ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Bangxian was summoned from Chuzhou and urged peace. Offending Tuozhou, he was demoted two ranks.

sentences.zh: 於是左司諫易袚、大理少卿陳景俊、太學博士錢廷玉皆起而言恢復之計矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon Left Secretariat Remonstrator Yi Ba, Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review Chen Jingjun, and Erudite of the Imperial Academy Qian Tingyu all rose and spoke of plans for recovery.
translations.idiomatic: Left Secretariat Remonstrator Yi Ba, Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review Chen Jingjun, and Imperial Academy Erudite Qian Tingyu now joined in advocating recovery of the north.

sentences.zh: 詔侂胄日一朝。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that Tuozhou hold daily audiences.
translations.idiomatic: An edict required Tuozhou to attend court daily.

sentences.zh: 友龍、叔似並升宣撫使。

translations.literal: Youlong and Shushi were both promoted to pacification commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Youlong and Xue Shushi were both promoted to pacification commissioners.

sentences.zh: 吳曦兼陝西、河東招撫使，皇甫斌副之。

translations.literal: Wu Xi was additionally made recruitment and pacification commissioner of Shaanxi and Hedong, with Huangfu Bin as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xi was also made recruitment and pacification commissioner of Shaanxi and Hedong, with Huangfu Bin as deputy.

sentences.zh: 時鎮江武鋒軍統制陳孝慶復泗州及虹縣，江州統制許進復新息縣，光州孫成復褒信縣。

translations.literal: At that time Commander of the Wufeng Army at Zhenjiang Chen Xiaoqing recovered Sizhou and Hong County; Commander at Jiang Prefecture Xu Jin recovered Xinxian County; Sun Cheng of Guang Prefecture recovered Baoxin County.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xiaoqing, commander of the Wufeng Army at Zhenjiang, recaptured Sizhou and Hong County. Xu Jin at Jiangzhou recaptured Xinxian, and Sun Cheng at Guangzhou recaptured Baoxin.

sentences.zh: 捷書聞，侂胄乃議降詔趣諸將進兵。

translations.literal: When the victory reports were heard, Tuozhou then discussed issuing an edict urging the generals to advance troops.
translations.idiomatic: When news of these victories arrived, Tuozhou proposed issuing an edict urging all generals to advance.

sentences.zh: 未幾，皇甫斌兵敗于唐州；

translations.literal: Before long, Huangfu Bin's troops were defeated at Tang Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Huangfu Bin's army was defeated at Tang Prefecture;

sentences.zh: 秦世輔至城固軍潰；

translations.literal: Qin Shifu reached Chenggu and the army collapsed;
translations.idiomatic: Qin Shifu's army collapsed upon reaching Chenggu;

sentences.zh: 郭倬、李汝翼敗於宿州，敵追圍倬，倬執統制田俊邁以遺敵，乃獲免。

translations.literal: Guo Chuo and Li Ruyi were defeated at Suzhou; the enemy pursued and besieged Chuo; Chuo seized the regimental commander Tian Junmai and sent him as a gift to the enemy, and only then escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Chuo and Li Ruyi were defeated at Suzhou. Pursued and surrounded, Guo Chuo handed over his commander Tian Junmai to the enemy and only thus escaped.

sentences.zh: 事聞，鄧友龍罷，以嶽丘峑代為宣撫使。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, Deng Youlong was dismissed and Yue Qiunan was substituted as pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When the news reached court, Deng Youlong was dismissed and Yue Qiunan replaced him as pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 侂胄既喪師，始覺為師旦所誤。

translations.literal: Tuozhou having already lost troops, only then realized he had been deceived by Shidan.
translations.idiomatic: After these defeats, Tuozhou finally realized Su Shidan had misled him.

sentences.zh: 侂胄招李壁飲酒，酒酣，語及師旦，壁微摘其過侂胄以為然。

translations.literal: Tuozhou invited Li Bi to drink; when the wine was deep, they spoke of Shidan; Bi subtly pointed out his faults and Tuozhou thought this correct.
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou invited Li Bi to drink. When the wine had loosened tongues, they spoke of Su Shidan. Li Bi gently listed Shidan's failings, and Tuozhou agreed.

sentences.zh: 壁乃悉數其罪，贊侂胄斥去之。

translations.literal: Bi then enumerated all his crimes and urged Tuozhou to expel him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bi then catalogued Shidan's crimes in full and persuaded Tuozhou to dismiss him.

sentences.zh: 翌日，師旦謫韶州，斬郭倬於京口，流李汝翼、王大節、李爽於嶺南。

translations.literal: The next day Shidan was demoted to Shaozhou; Guo Chuo was beheaded at Jingkou; Li Ruyi, Wang Dajie, and Li Shuang were exiled to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Su Shidan was demoted to Shaozhou. Guo Chuo was beheaded at Jingkou, and Li Ruyi, Wang Dajie, and Li Shuang were exiled to the far south.

sentences.zh: 已而金人渡淮，攻廬、和、真、揚，取安豐、濠，又攻襄陽，至棗陽，乃以丘峑僉書樞密院事，督視江、淮軍馬。

translations.literal: Before long the Jurchens crossed the Huai, attacked Lu, He, Zhen, and Yang, took Anfeng and Hao, also attacked Xiangyang and reached Zaoyang; then Yue Qiunan was made vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs to supervise Jiang-Huai military forces.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Jurchens crossed the Huai, attacking Lu, He, Zhen, and Yang, capturing Anfeng and Hao, and pressing toward Xiangyang as far as Zaoyang. Yue Qiunan was appointed vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs to oversee troops on the Jiang-Huai front.

sentences.zh: 侂胄輸家財二十萬以助軍，而諭丘峑募人持書幣赴敵營，謂用兵乃蘇師旦、鄧友龍、皇甫斌所為，非朝廷意。

translations.literal: Tuozhou contributed two hundred thousand of his household wealth to aid the army, and instructed Qiunan to recruit men to carry letters and gifts to the enemy camp, saying the use of troops was the doing of Su Shidan, Deng Youlong, and Huangfu Bin, not the court's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou contributed two hundred thousand cash from his family fortune to the war effort and instructed Yue Qiunan to send envoys to the Jurchen camp claiming that the war had been the work of Su Shidan, Deng Youlong, and Huangfu Bin—not the court's will.

sentences.zh: 金人答書辭甚倨，且多所要索，謂侂胄無意用兵，師旦等安得專。

translations.literal: The Jurchens' reply letter was very arrogant in tone and contained many demands, saying Tuozhou had no intent to use troops—how could Shidan and the others act on their own?
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchen reply was haughty and laden with demands. They asked how Su Shidan and the others could have acted alone if Tuozhou had not wanted war.

sentences.zh: 峑又遣書許還淮北流民及今年歲幣，金人乃有許意。

translations.literal: Qiunan again sent a letter promising to return refugees north of the Huai and this year's annual tribute; the Jurchens then showed willingness to agree.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Qiunan sent another letter offering to return Huai-north refugees and pay the year's tribute. The Jurchens then showed willingness to negotiate.

sentences.zh: 會招撫使郭倪與金人戰，敗於六合；

translations.literal: It happened that Recruitment Commissioner Guo Ni fought the Jurchens and was defeated at Liuhe;
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Recruitment Commissioner Guo Ni fought the Jurchens and was defeated at Liuhe;

sentences.zh: 金人攻蜀，吳曦叛，受金命稱蜀王。

translations.literal: The Jurchens attacked Shu; Wu Xi rebelled and, accepting Jurchen orders, styled himself King of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens attacked Sichuan. Wu Xi rebelled and, at their command, declared himself King of Shu.

sentences.zh: 峑乞移書敵營伸前議，且謂金人指太師平章為首謀，宜免系銜。

translations.literal: Qiunan begged to send a letter to the enemy camp expanding on the earlier discussion, and said the Jurchens pointed to the Grand Preceptor and Director as the chief plotter—his title should be removed from the letter.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Qiunan asked to write again to the enemy camp, reiterating the earlier offer, and argued that since the Jurchens named the Grand Preceptor and director of state affairs as the chief instigator, Tuozhou's titles should be omitted from any correspondence.

sentences.zh: 侂胄忿，峑坐罷。

translations.literal: Tuozhou was resentful; Qiunan was dismissed on this charge.
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou was enraged, and Yue Qiunan was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 曦反狀聞，舉朝震駭。

translations.literal: When Xi's rebellion was reported, the whole court was shaken with alarm.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Xi's rebellion was reported, the entire court was shaken.

sentences.zh: 侂胄亟遺曦書，許以茅土之封，書未達而安內、楊巨源已率義士誅曦矣。

translations.literal: Tuozhou urgently sent Xi a letter promising enfeoffment with domain and fief; the letter had not arrived when An Nei and Yang Juyuan had already led loyal men to execute Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou urgently wrote Wu Xi offering him a feudal domain, but before the letter arrived, An Nei and Yang Juyuan had already led loyal troops to kill him.

sentences.zh: 侂胄連遣方信孺使北請和，以林拱辰為通謝使。

translations.literal: Tuozhou repeatedly sent Fang Xinru as envoy north to seek peace, with Lin Gongchen as envoy of thanks and communication.
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou sent Fang Xinru north repeatedly to sue for peace, with Lin Gongchen as envoy of acknowledgment.

sentences.zh: 金人欲責正隆以前禮賂，以侵疆為界，且索犒軍銀凡數千萬，而縛送首議用兵之臣。

translations.literal: The Jurchens wished to hold Song accountable for gifts before the Zhenglong era, take the contested territory as the border, and moreover demand reward silver for the army totaling tens of millions, while binding and sending the chief ministers who first proposed using troops.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens demanded retroactive tribute payments from before the Zhenglong era, a border drawn at occupied territory, war indemnities totaling tens of millions in silver, and the handover of the officials who had first advocated war.

sentences.zh: 信孺歸，白事朝堂，不敢斥言，侂胄窮其說，乃微及之。

translations.literal: Xinru returned and reported the matter at court, not daring to speak explicitly; Tuozhou pressed his account and only then did it slightly touch on this.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xinru returned and reported to the court, too afraid to speak plainly. Only when Tuozhou pressed him did he hint at these demands.

sentences.zh: 侂胄大怒，和議遂輟。

translations.literal: Tuozhou was greatly enraged and peace talks were then halted.
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou was furious, and peace negotiations broke off.

sentences.zh: 起辛棄疾為樞密都承旨。

translations.literal: Xin Qiji was raised to director of the Bureau of Military Affairs staff.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Qiji was recalled and appointed director of the Bureau of Military Affairs staff.

sentences.zh: 會棄疾死，乃以殿前副都指揮使趙淳為江、淮制置使，復銳意用兵。

translations.literal: It happened that Qiji died; then Deputy Commander-in-Chief of the Palace Front Zhao Chun was made Jiang-Huai military commissioner, and again keen intent to use troops.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Qiji died soon after. Zhao Chun, deputy commander-in-chief of the Palace Front, was appointed Jiang-Huai military commissioner, and Tuozhou again pressed for war.

sentences.zh: 自兵興以來，蜀口、漢、淮之民死於兵戈者，不可勝計，公私之力大屈，而侂胄意猶未已，中外憂懼。

translations.literal: Since troops were raised, the people of Shukou, Han, and the Huai who died by arms cannot be fully counted; public and private strength was greatly exhausted, yet Tuozhou's intent was still not ceased—inside and outside all were anxious and fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Since the war began, countless civilians in Sichuan, Hanzhong, and the Huai region had died in the fighting. Public and private resources were exhausted, yet Tuozhou still would not relent. Alarm spread through court and country alike.

sentences.zh: 禮部侍郎史彌遠，時兼資善堂翊善，謀誅侂胄，議甚秘，皇子榮王入奏，楊皇后亦從中力請，乃得密旨。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Rites Shi Miyuan, who then also served as assistant tutor at the Hall for Nurturing Goodness, plotted to execute Tuozhou; the discussion was very secret; the prince Rong Wang entered to memorialize; Empress Yang also joined from within with forceful pleading—only then was a secret edict obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Rites Shi Miyuan, who also served as tutor at the Hall for Nurturing Goodness, plotted to kill Tuozhou in deepest secrecy. Prince Rong entered a memorial, and Empress Yang added her urgent plea from within the palace. A secret edict was at last obtained.

sentences.zh: 彌遠以告參知政事錢象祖、李壁。

translations.literal: Miyuan told this to Vice Grand Councillors Qian Xiangzu and Li Bi.
translations.idiomatic: Miyuan confided in Vice Grand Councillors Qian Xiangzu and Li Bi.

sentences.zh: 御筆云：「韓侂胄久任國柄，輕啟兵端，使南北生靈枉罹凶害，可罷平章軍國事，與在外宮觀。

translations.literal: The emperor's brush stated: "Han Tuozhou long held state power, lightly opened military conflict, causing living beings north and south to suffer wrongful slaughter—he may be dismissed from director of military and state affairs and given an outside palace commission.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's own hand decreed: "Han Tuozhou has long wielded state power and recklessly provoked war, bringing wrongful death to countless people north and south. He is dismissed from the directorate of military and state affairs and assigned an outside palace commission.

sentences.zh: 陳自強阿附充位，不恤國事，可罷右丞相。

translations.literal: Chen Ziqiang fawned and filled his post, not caring for state affairs—he may be dismissed from right chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Ziqiang has clung to office through flattery and neglected state affairs. He is dismissed from the right chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 日下出國門。

translations.literal: They shall leave the capital gate this day."
translations.idiomatic: They are to leave the capital this day."

sentences.zh: 」仍令權主管殿前司公事夏震以兵三百防護。

translations.literal: It still ordered Acting Supervisor of Palace Front Affairs Xia Zhen to use three hundred soldiers as escort and guard.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time, Acting Supervisor of Palace Front Affairs Xia Zhen was ordered to escort them with three hundred soldiers.

sentences.zh: 象祖欲奏審，壁謂事留恐泄，不可。

translations.literal: Xiangzu wished to submit for review; Bi said that if the matter lingered there was fear of leakage and it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Xiangzu wanted to submit the edict for formal review, but Li Bi warned that delay risked exposure and must be avoided.

sentences.zh: 翌日，侂胄入朝，震呵止於途，擁至玉津園側殛殺之。

translations.literal: The next day Tuozhou entered for court audience; Zhen shouted to stop him on the road, escorted him to the side of Yujin Garden and executed him on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Tuozhou came to court. Xia Zhen halted him on the road, escorted him to the edge of Yujin Garden, and had him killed on the spot.

sentences.zh: 先一日，周筠謂侂胄，事將不善，侂胄與自強謀用林行可為諫議大夫，盡擊謀侂胄者。

translations.literal: One day before, Zhou Yun told Tuozhou that matters would turn bad; Tuozhou and Ziqiang plotted to use Lin Xingke as Remonstrance and Discussion Grandee to strike at all who plotted against Tuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: The day before, Zhou Yun warned Tuozhou that trouble was brewing. Tuozhou and Chen Ziqiang plotted to appoint Lin Xingke remonstrance grandee and purge all who conspired against him.

sentences.zh: 是日，行可方請對，自強坐待漏院，語同列曰：「今日大坡上殿。

translations.literal: That day Xingke was just requesting audience; Ziqiang sat in the Office of Awaiting the Leak and told his colleagues: "Today the great slope ascend the hall.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Lin Xingke was requesting audience. Chen Ziqiang, waiting in the antechamber, told his colleagues, "Today's the big day—we ascend the hall.

sentences.zh: 」俄侂胄先驅至，象祖色變。

translations.literal: " Before long Tuozhou's vanguard arrived; Xiangzu's countenance changed.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon Tuozhou's advance guard appeared. Qian Xiangzu's face went pale.

sentences.zh: 尋報侂胄已押出，象祖乃入奏。

translations.literal: Soon it was reported that Tuozhou had already been escorted out; Xiangzu then entered to memorialize.
translations.idiomatic: Moments later word came that Tuozhou had been seized and removed. Qian Xiangzu then entered to present the edict.

sentences.zh: 有詔斬蘇師旦於廣東。

translations.literal: There was an edict to behead Su Shidan in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Su Shidan beheaded in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 嘉定元年，金人求函侂胄首，乃命臨安府斫侂胄棺，取其首遺之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiading, the Jurchens asked for Tuozhou's head in a box; then Lin'an Prefecture was ordered to hew open Tuozhou's coffin, take his head and send it as gift.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jiading, the Jurchens demanded Tuozhou's head in a box. The Lin'an prefecture was ordered to open his coffin and send his head to them.

sentences.zh: 侂胄用事十四年，威行宮省，權震寓內。

translations.literal: Tuozhou wielded power fourteen years; authority extended through palace and ministries, power shook the realm within.
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou had held power for fourteen years. His authority dominated the palace and ministries, and his influence shook the empire.

sentences.zh: 嘗鑿山為園，下瞰宗廟。

translations.literal: He once carved a mountain into a garden, overlooking the imperial ancestral temple from above.
translations.idiomatic: He had carved out a hillside garden that looked down upon the imperial ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 出入宮闈無度。

translations.literal: Entering and leaving the palace precincts without measure.
translations.idiomatic: He came and went within the palace without restraint.

sentences.zh: 孝宗疇昔思政之所，偃然居之，老宮人見之往往垂涕。

translations.literal: At the place where Xiaozong in former days had pondered governance, he reclined at ease and dwelt there; old palace women seeing this often shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: He occupied at ease the very chambers where Emperor Xiaozong had once pondered state affairs. Elder palace women who saw this often wept.

sentences.zh: 顏郐或草制，言其得聖之清。

translations.literal: Yan Yu once drafted an edict and spoke of his obtaining the sage's purity.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Yu once drafted an edict praising Tuozhou as attaining the sage's purity.

sentences.zh: 易袚撰答詔，以元聖褒之。

translations.literal: Yi Ba composed the reply edict and with "primordial sage" praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Ba drafted the imperial reply, extolling him as a primordial sage.

sentences.zh: 四方投書獻頌者，謂伊、霍、旦、奭不足以似其勳，有稱為「我王」者。

translations.literal: Those throughout the four directions who submitted letters and presented praise said Yi Yin, Huo Guang, Duke of Zhou, and Duke of Shao were insufficient to resemble his merit; some styled him "Our King."
translations.idiomatic: Petitioners from across the realm declared that Yi Yin, Huo Guang, the Duke of Zhou, and the Duke of Shao could not compare with his achievements. Some even called him "Our King."

sentences.zh: 余𡕇請加九錫，趙師𢍰乞置平原郡王府官屬。

translations.literal: Yu Yao requested adding the Nine Bestowals; Zhao Shibo begged to establish officials for the Prince of Pingyuan Commandery's household.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yao requested that Tuozhou be granted the Nine Bestowals, and Zhao Shibo asked that a full staff be appointed for his Pingyuan princely household.

sentences.zh: 侂胄皆當之不辭。

translations.literal: Tuozhou in every case accepted without declining.
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou accepted every such honor without demur.

sentences.zh: 所嬖妾張、譚、王、陳皆封郡國夫人，號「四夫人」，每內宴，與妃嬪雜坐，恃勢驕倨，掖庭皆惡之；

translations.literal: His favored concubines Zhang, Tan, Wang, and Chen were all enfeoffed as ladies of commanderies and states, styled the "Four Ladies"; at each inner banquet they sat mixed with imperial consorts, relying on power with arrogant insolence—the rear palace all hated them;
translations.idiomatic: His favored concubines—the Zhang, Tan, Wang, and Chen women—were all enfeoffed as ladies of commanderies and states and styled the "Four Ladies." At palace banquets they sat indiscriminately among imperial consorts, insufferably arrogant. Everyone in the inner quarters despised them;

sentences.zh: 其下，受封者尤眾。

translations.literal: Below them, those receiving enfeoffment were especially numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Below them, still more women received noble titles.

sentences.zh: 至是，論四夫人罪，或杖或徒，餘數十人縱遣之。

translations.literal: By this time their crimes were adjudged; the Four Ladies were either beaten or penal servitude; the remaining several tens were released and sent away.
translations.idiomatic: Now their crimes were prosecuted. The Four Ladies were flogged or sent to penal servitude, and several dozen others were released and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 有司籍其家，多乘輿服御之飾，其僭紊極矣。

translations.literal: The responsible officials inventoried their households; many had ornaments of imperial carriage and attire—their presumption and disorder reached the extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Officials inventoried their households and found many possessions fit only for imperial use. Their presumption had reached the utmost.

sentences.zh: 始，侂胄以導達中外之言，遂見寵任。

translations.literal: At the beginning, Tuozhou because he conveyed and communicated words inside and outside gained favored appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In the beginning, Tuozhou had won favor by serving as the empress's liaison to the court.

sentences.zh: 朱熹、彭龜年既以論侂胄去，貴戚吳琚語人曰：「帝初無固留侂胄意，使有一人繼言之，去之易爾。

translations.literal: After Xi and Peng Guinian had both been removed for criticizing Tuozhou, the imperial relative Wu Ju told someone: "The emperor at first had no fixed intent to keep Tuozhou; if one person had followed in speaking, removing him would have been easy.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhu Xi and Peng Guinian were dismissed for criticizing Tuozhou, the imperial kinsman Wu Ju remarked, "The emperor never firmly meant to keep Tuozhou. Had even one more official spoken up, dismissing him would have been easy.

sentences.zh: 而一時台諫及執政大臣多其党與，故稔其惡以底大僇。

translations.literal: Yet for a time the censorial remonstrators and chief ministers were mostly his faction and associates, and therefore his evil ripened until the great punishment."
translations.idiomatic: But censors and chief ministers at the time were mostly his allies, so his wickedness only deepened until it brought him to ruin."

sentences.zh: 開禧用兵，帝意弗善也。

translations.literal: When Kaixi troops were used, the emperor's intent was not good toward it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor never approved of the Kaixi war.

sentences.zh: 侂胄死，甯宗諭大臣曰：「恢復豈非美事，但不量力爾。」

translations.literal: When Tuozhou died, Ningzong instructed the great ministers: "Recovery—is it not a fine matter? Only he did not measure his strength."
translations.idiomatic: After Tuozhou's death, Emperor Ningzong told his ministers, "Recovering lost territory is a worthy goal—but he failed to measure his strength."

sentences.zh: 侂胄娶憲聖吳皇后姪女，無子，取魯𡬐子為後，名㣉，既誅侂胄，削籍流沙門島云。

translations.literal: Tuozhou married Empress Dowager Xiansheng Wu's grandniece. Having no sons, he took Lu Shuo's son as his heir, named Kan. After Tuozhou was executed, [the heir] was struck from the registers and [sent] to Liushamen Island, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou had married a grandniece of Empress Dowager Xiansheng Wu. Childless, he adopted the son of Lu Shuo as his heir and named him Kan. When Tuozhou was put to death, the boy was removed from the rolls and banished to Liushamen Island, or so it is recorded.

sentences.zh: 丁大全

translations.literal: Ding Daquan
translations.idiomatic: Ding Daquan

sentences.zh: 丁大全字子萬，鎮江人。

translations.literal: Ding Daquan, courtesy name Ziwan, was a man of Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Daquan, styled Ziwan, was a native of Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 面藍色。

translations.literal: His face was bluish in color.
translations.idiomatic: His complexion was bluish.

sentences.zh: 嘉熙二年舉進士，調蕭山尉。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiaxi he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed Assistant Magistrate of Xiaoshan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1238 he passed the jinshi examination and was posted as assistant magistrate of Xiaoshan.

sentences.zh: 上謁帥閫，安撫使史岩之俟眾賓退，獨留大全，款曲甚至，期以他日必大用。

translations.literal: When he went up to pay respects at the command headquarters, the Pacification Commissioner Shi Yanzhi waited until all the other guests had withdrawn, kept Daquan alone, treated him with exceptional intimacy, and promised that on another day he would surely be greatly employed.
translations.idiomatic: On a visit to the regional command, Pacification Commissioner Shi Yanzhi waited until the other guests had left, then kept Daquan behind and treated him with unusual warmth, assuring him that he would one day be given great office.

sentences.zh: 大全為戚裏婢婿，寅緣以取寵位。

translations.literal: Daquan was the son-in-law of a maid in the imperial kin, and by such connections sought favor and rank.
translations.idiomatic: Daquan had married the daughter of a maidservant in the imperial clan, and he climbed to favor and office through such connections.

sentences.zh: 事內侍盧允升、董宋臣。

translations.literal: He served the eunuchs Lu Yunsheng and Dong Songchen.
translations.idiomatic: He attached himself to the eunuchs Lu Yunsheng and Dong Songchen.

sentences.zh: 累官為大理司直、添差通判饒州。

translations.literal: Through successive appointments he became Direct Clerk of the Court of Judicial Review and Supernumerary Vice Commissioner of Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to direct clerk in the Court of Judicial Review and supernumerary vice commissioner of Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 入為太府寺簿，調尚書茶鹽所檢閱江州分司，復兼樞密院編修官。

translations.literal: He entered [the capital] as Clerk of the Office of the Imperial Treasury, was transferred to be Review Clerk at the Jiangzhou branch of the Ministry of Revenue's Tea and Salt Office, and again concurrently served as Compiler in the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as a clerk in the Office of the Imperial Treasury, was transferred to review clerk at the Jiangzhou branch of the tea and salt bureau, and again served concurrently as a compiler in the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 拜右正言兼侍講，辭。

translations.literal: He was appointed Right Direct Remonstrator and concurrently Lecturer, but declined.
translations.idiomatic: He was offered the posts of right direct remonstrator and lecturer but declined them.

sentences.zh: 改右司諫，拜殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: He was changed to Right Remonstrator of the Department of State Affairs and appointed Attendant Censor within the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as right remonstrator in the Department of State Affairs and appointed attendant censor within the palace.

sentences.zh: 升侍御史兼侍讀。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Attendant Censor and concurrently Lector.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to attendant censor and concurrent lector.

sentences.zh: 劾奏丞相董槐，章未下，大全夜半調隅兵百餘人，露刃圍槐第，以台牒驅迫之出，紿令輿槐至大理寺，欲以此恐之。

translations.literal: He impeached and memorialized against Chief Councillor Dong Huai. Before the memorial was issued, in the middle of the night Daquan mobilized over a hundred local guards, bared their blades, and surrounded Huai's residence. Using an order from the Censorate he drove and coerced Huai out, falsely ordering a sedan to convey Huai to the Court of Judicial Review, intending to frighten him with this.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Chief Councillor Dong Huai, but before the memorial could be issued, Daquan summoned more than a hundred local guards in the dead of night, drew their blades, and surrounded Huai's house. With a writ from the Censorate he forced Huai out, then falsely ordered a sedan to carry him to the Court of Judicial Review, hoping to terrify him.

sentences.zh: 須臾，出北關，棄槐，嘂呼而散。

translations.literal: After a short while they went out through the North Gate, abandoned Huai, shouted, and dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: A moment later they passed through the North Gate, left Huai behind, shouted, and scattered.

sentences.zh: 槐徐步入接待寺，罷相之命下矣。

translations.literal: Huai slowly walked into the Reception Temple; the order for his dismissal as chief councillor had already been issued.
translations.idiomatic: Huai walked unhurriedly into the Reception Temple—the order removing him as chief councillor had already arrived.

sentences.zh: 自是志氣驕傲，道路以目。

translations.literal: From then on his spirit grew arrogant and proud; on the roads people looked only with their eyes.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he grew insufferably arrogant, and people in the streets dared only glance at him in silence.
