sentences.zh: 尋為右諫議大夫，進端明殿學士、僉書樞密院事，封丹陽郡侯，進同知樞密院事兼權參知政事。

translations.literal: Soon he became Right Remonstration Grandee, was promoted to Academician of the Duanming Hall and Junior Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, enfeoffed as Marquis of Danyang, and further promoted to Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs and concurrently Acting Assistant Chief Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made right remonstration grandee, then promoted to academician of the Duanming Hall and junior director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, enfeoffed as marquis of Danyang, and further raised to vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs with acting assistant chief councillor.

sentences.zh: 寶祐六年，拜參知政事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Baoyou he was appointed Assistant Chief Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1258 he was appointed assistant chief councillor.

sentences.zh: 四月，拜右丞相兼樞密使，進封公。

translations.literal: In the fourth month he was appointed Right Chief Councillor and concurrently Commissioner of Military Affairs, and was advanced in enfeoffment to Duke.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he became right chief councillor and commissioner of military affairs, and was raised in rank to duke.

sentences.zh: 初，大全以袁疴為九江制置副使，疴貪且刻，逮系漁湖土豪，督促輸錢甚急。

translations.literal: Initially Daquan had appointed Yuan Ke as Vice Military Commissioner of Jiujiang. Ke was greedy and harsh; he arrested and imprisoned local magnates of the fishing lakes and urgently compelled them to pay money.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Daquan had made Yuan Ke vice military commissioner of Jiujiang. Ke was greedy and cruel: he seized local strongmen on the fishing lakes and pressed them relentlessly for money.

sentences.zh: 土豪怒，盡以魚舟濟北來之兵。

translations.literal: The local magnates were enraged and used all their fishing boats to ferry the troops coming from the north.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, the local magnates used every fishing boat they had to ferry the northern invaders across the water.

sentences.zh: 太學生陳宗、劉黼、黃鏞、曾唯、陳宜中、林則祖等六人，伏闕上書訟大全。

translations.literal: Six students of the Imperial Academy—Chen Zong, Liu Fu, Huang Yong, Zeng Wei, Chen Yizhong, and Lin Zzezu—prostrated themselves before the palace gate and submitted a memorial accusing Daquan.
translations.idiomatic: Six students of the Imperial Academy—Chen Zong, Liu Fu, Huang Yong, Zeng Wei, Chen Yizhong, and Lin Zzezu—knelt at the palace gate and submitted a memorial denouncing Daquan.

sentences.zh: 台臣翁應弼、吳衍為大全鷹犬，鈐制學校，貶逐宗等。

translations.literal: The censorial officials Weng Yingbi and Wu Yan were Daquan's hawk-dogs; they controlled and restrained the schools and demoted and banished Zong and the others.
translations.idiomatic: The censors Weng Yingbi and Wu Yan served as Daquan's henchmen: they muzzled the academies and had Zong and his fellows demoted and banished.

sentences.zh: 明年，監察御史劉應龍請加竄，追削兩官，移竄貴州團練使。

translations.literal: The next year Supervising Censor Liu Yinglong requested additional banishment: two ranks were posthumously stripped, and he was further banished to Military Training Commissioner of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Supervising Censor Liu Yinglong asked that Daquan be punished more severely: two ranks were retroactively stripped, and he was banished to serve as military training commissioner in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 與州守游翁明失色杯酒間，翁明訴大全陰造弓矢，將通蠻為不軌。

translations.literal: While drinking with the Prefect You Wengming, [Daquan] turned pale over the wine cups. Wengming reported that Daquan had secretly manufactured bows and arrows and intended to join with the barbarians in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Over wine with Prefect You Wengming, Daquan turned pale. Wengming then accused him of secretly making bows and arrows and plotting with the barbarians to rebel.

sentences.zh: 朱禩孫以聞于朝。

translations.literal: Zhu Shunsun reported this to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Shunsun reported the matter to the court.

sentences.zh: 又明年，移置新州。

translations.literal: Again the next year, he was transferred to Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The year after that he was transferred to Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 太常少卿兼權直舍人院劉震孫繳奏乞移徙海島。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Acting Drafting Officer of the Academy of Palace Deliberations Liu Zhensun submitted a rescript petition requesting that he be moved to an island in the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhensun, vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and acting drafting officer of the Academy of Palace Deliberations, returned the memorial with a request that Daquan be sent to an island in the sea.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，將官畢遷護送，舟過藤州，擠之于水而死。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year the military officer Bi Qian was assigned to escort him. When the boat passed Tengzhou, [Bi Qian] pushed him into the water and he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year the officer Bi Qian was assigned to escort him. When the boat reached Tengzhou, Bi Qian pushed him into the water and drowned him.

sentences.zh: 大全知淮西，總領鄭羽富甲吳門，始欲結姻，羽不從。

translations.literal: When Daquan was Military Commissioner of Huai West, the Chief Quartermaster Zheng Yu was the wealthiest man at Wu Gate. At first [Daquan] wanted to marry into his family; Yu refused.
translations.idiomatic: While Daquan governed Huai West, Chief Quartermaster Zheng Yu was the richest man in Suzhou. Daquan first sought a marriage alliance with his family, but Yu refused.

sentences.zh: 遂令台臣卓夢卿彈之，籍其家。

translations.literal: Thereupon he had the censorial official Zhuo Mengqing impeach him and confiscated his family property.
translations.idiomatic: Daquan then had censor Zhuo Mengqing impeach him and confiscate his estate.

sentences.zh: 為子壽翁聘婦，見其豔，自取，為世所醜。

translations.literal: He betrothed a wife for his son Shou Weng; when he saw how beautiful she was, he took her for himself—an act condemned by the world.
translations.idiomatic: He arranged a bride for his son Shou Weng, but when he saw how beautiful she was he took her for himself—a deed universally despised.

sentences.zh: 賈似道

translations.literal: Jia Sidao
translations.idiomatic: Jia Sidao

sentences.zh: 賈似道字師憲，台州人，制置使涉之子也。

translations.literal: Jia Sidao, courtesy name Shixian, was a man of Taizhou and the son of Military Commissioner She.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Sidao, styled Shixian, was a native of Taizhou and the son of Military Commissioner Jia She.

sentences.zh: 少落魄，為遊博，不事操行。

translations.literal: In youth he was down and out, given to wandering and gambling, and did not cultivate moral conduct.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he was shiftless, given to roaming and gambling, and cared nothing for proper conduct.

sentences.zh: 以父蔭補嘉興司倉。

translations.literal: Through his father's yin privilege he was appointed Grain Storehouse Officer of Jiaxing.
translations.idiomatic: Through his father's privilege of office he received appointment as grain storehouse officer in Jiaxing.

sentences.zh: 會其姊入宮，有寵于理宗，為貴妃，遂詔赴廷對，妃於內中奉湯藥以給之。

translations.literal: When his elder sister entered the palace and won favor with Emperor Lizong as an imperial consort, he was thereupon ordered to come for an imperial audience. The consort within the inner palace supplied him with soup and medicine.
translations.idiomatic: When his elder sister entered the palace and became a favored consort of Emperor Lizong, Sidao was summoned for an imperial audience. From within the inner quarters she sent him soup and medicine to sustain him.

sentences.zh: 擢太常丞、軍器監。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Supervisor of the Armaments Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and supervisor of the Armaments Directorate.

sentences.zh: 益恃寵不檢，日縱游諸妓家，至夜即燕遊湖上不反。

translations.literal: He relied increasingly on favor and did not restrain himself. Day after day he roamed the houses of courtesans; at night he would feast and wander on West Lake and not return.
translations.idiomatic: Growing bolder in his favor, he abandoned all restraint. By day he wandered from brothel to brothel; by night he feasted on West Lake and did not come home.

sentences.zh: 理宗嘗夜憑高，望西湖中燈火異常時，語左右曰：「此必似道也。

translations.literal: Emperor Lizong once at night leaned on the heights and gazed at West Lake; the lights on the water were unlike any ordinary time. He said to those beside him: "This must be Sidao."
translations.idiomatic: One night Emperor Lizong looked down from a height at West Lake and saw lights on the water unlike any ordinary night. He said to those around him, "That must be Sidao."

sentences.zh: 」明日詢之果然，使京尹史岩之戒敕之。

translations.literal: The next day he inquired and it was indeed so. He had Capital Magistrate Shi Yanzhi admonish and warn him.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he asked and found it was indeed so. He had the capital magistrate Shi Yanzhi warn and admonish him.

sentences.zh: 岩之曰：「似道雖有少年氣習，然其材可大用也。

translations.literal: Yanzhi said: "Although Sidao has youthful habits, his talent can be greatly employed."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yanzhi replied, "Sidao may still have the habits of youth, but his talent is fit for great employment."

sentences.zh: 」尋出知澧州。

translations.literal: Soon he was sent out as Prefect of Lizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was sent out to serve as prefect of Lizhou.

sentences.zh: 淳祐元年，改湖廣總領。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chunyou he was changed to Chief Quartermaster of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1241 he was reassigned as chief quartermaster of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 三年，加戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the third year he was given the additional title of Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he received the additional title of vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 五年，以寶章閣直學士為沿江制置副使、知江州兼江西路安撫使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, with the title of Direct Academician of the Baozhang Pavilion, he became Vice Military Commissioner of the Yangzi River line, Prefect of Jiangzhou, and concurrently Pacification Commissioner of Jiangxi Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, as direct academician of the Baozhang Pavilion, he became vice military commissioner on the Yangzi line, prefect of Jiangzhou, and pacification commissioner of Jiangxi Circuit.

sentences.zh: 一歲中，再遷京湖制置使兼知江陵府，調度賞罰，得以便宜施行。

translations.literal: Within one year he was promoted twice—to Military Commissioner of Jinghu and concurrently Prefect of Jiangling—with authority to issue rewards and punishments at his discretion.
translations.idiomatic: Within a single year he was promoted twice, to military commissioner of Jinghu and concurrently prefect of Jiangling, with authority to reward and punish as he saw fit.

sentences.zh: 九年，加寶文閣學士、京湖安撫制置大使。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was given the additional titles of Academician of the Baowen Pavilion and Grand Pacification and Military Commissioner of Jinghu.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he received the additional titles of academician of the Baowen Pavilion and grand pacification and military commissioner of Jinghu.

sentences.zh: 十年，以端明殿學士移鎮兩淮，年始三十餘。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, as Academician of the Duanming Hall, he was transferred to command Liang Huai; he was then just over thirty years old.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, as academician of the Duanming Hall, he was transferred to command the Two Huai regions—he was then barely past thirty.

sentences.zh: 寶祐二年，加同知樞密院事、臨海郡開國公，威權日盛。

translations.literal: In the second year of Baoyou he was given the additional posts of Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Duke of the Commandery of Linhai; his power and authority grew daily.
translations.idiomatic: In 1254 he was made vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs and duke of Linhai commandery, and his power grew day by day.

sentences.zh: 台諫嘗論其二部將，即毅然求去。

translations.literal: When censors remonstrated about two of his subordinate generals, he at once resolutely requested to leave office.
translations.idiomatic: When the censors criticized two of his subordinate generals, he immediately and firmly asked to resign.

sentences.zh: 孫子秀新除淮東總領，外人忽傳似道已密奏不可矣，丞相董槐懼，留身請之，帝以為無有，槐終不敢遣子秀，以似道所善陸壑代之，其見憚已如此。

translations.literal: Sun Zixiu had newly been appointed Chief Quartermaster of Huai East. Outsiders suddenly spread word that Sidao had already secretly memorialized that he was unsuitable. Chief Councillor Dong Huai was alarmed, stayed behind to ask the emperor, who said there was nothing of the sort. Huai ultimately did not dare send Zixiu and replaced him with Lu He, whom Sidao favored—such was the dread he inspired.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Zixiu had just been appointed chief quartermaster of Huai East when rumor spread that Sidao had secretly memorialized against him. Chief Councillor Dong Huai was alarmed and stayed behind to ask the emperor, who said there was no such memorial. Huai still dared not send Sun Zixiu and substituted Lu He, whom Sidao favored—such was the fear he inspired.

sentences.zh: 四年，加參知政事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was given the additional post of Assistant Chief Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was made assistant chief councillor.

sentences.zh: 五年，加知樞密院事。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was given the additional post of Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was made director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 六年，改兩淮宣撫大使。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was changed to Grand Pacification Commissioner of Liang Huai.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was reassigned as grand pacification commissioner of the Two Huai regions.

sentences.zh: 自端平初，孟珙帥師會大元兵共滅金，約以陳、蔡為界。

translations.literal: From the beginning of Duanping, Meng Gong led troops in concert with Great Yuan forces to jointly destroy Jin, with the agreement that Chen and Cai would be the border.
translations.idiomatic: From the start of the Duanping era, Meng Gong had led troops alongside the Great Yuan army to destroy Jin, with Chen and Cai agreed as the boundary.

sentences.zh: 師未還而用趙範謀，發兵據殽、函，絕河津，取中原地，大元兵擊敗之，範僅以數千人遁歸。

translations.literal: Before the army had returned they adopted Zhao Fan's plan, sent troops to occupy Xiao and Han, cut off river crossings, and seize Central Plains territory. Great Yuan troops defeated them; Fan escaped back with only a few thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Before the army had even returned, the court followed Zhao Fan's plan and sent troops to seize Xiao and Han, block the river crossings, and take land in the Central Plains. The Great Yuan army routed them, and Fan fled home with only a few thousand men.

sentences.zh: 追兵至，問曰：「何為而敗盟也？

translations.literal: Pursuing troops arrived and asked: "For what reason did you break the alliance?"
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing troops arrived and demanded, "Why have you broken the alliance?"

sentences.zh: 」遂縱攻淮、漢，自是兵端大啟。

translations.literal: Thereupon they launched attacks on Huai and Han; from then on warfare on a large scale began.
translations.idiomatic: They then swept into the Huai and Han regions, and from that point full-scale war began.

sentences.zh: 開慶初，憲宗皇帝自將征蜀，世祖皇帝時以皇弟攻鄂州，元帥兀良哈台由雲南入交沚，自邕州蹂廣西，破湖南，傳檄數宋背盟之罪。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiqing, Emperor Xianzong of Yuan personally led a campaign against Shu. At that time Emperor Shizu, as imperial younger brother, attacked Ezhou. Marshal Uriyangqadai entered Jiaozhi via Yunnan, from Yongzhou ravaged Guangxi, broke into Hunan, and issued a proclamation enumerating Song's crimes for betraying the alliance.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Kaiqing era, Emperor Xianzong of Yuan personally led an expedition against Shu while the future Emperor Shizu, then a royal prince, attacked Ezhou. Marshal Uriyangqadai entered Jiaozhi through Yunnan, from Yongzhou ravaged Guangxi, broke into Hunan, and issued a proclamation listing Song's crimes for breaking the alliance.

sentences.zh: 理宗大懼，乃以趙葵軍信州，禦廣兵；

translations.literal: Emperor Lizong was greatly frightened. He dispatched Zhao Kui's army to Xinzhou to hold off the Guangxi troops;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Lizong was terrified. He sent Zhao Kui's army to Xinzhou to block the Guangxi force;

sentences.zh: 以似道軍漢陽，援鄂，即軍中拜右丞相。

translations.literal: and Sidao's army to Hanyang to reinforce Ezhou. Sidao was appointed Right Chief Councillor right there in the army.
translations.idiomatic: and Sidao's army to Hanyang to relieve Ezhou, appointing Sidao right there in camp as right chief councillor.

sentences.zh: 十月，鄂東南陬破，宋人再築，再破之，賴高達率諸將力戰。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the southeast corner of Ezhou was breached. The Song people rebuilt it; it was breached again. They relied on Gao Da leading the various generals in strenuous battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the southeast corner of Ezhou was breached. The Song rebuilt it, and it was breached again. Only Gao Da leading the generals in fierce fighting held the line.

sentences.zh: 似道時自漢陽入督師。

translations.literal: At that time Sidao himself entered from Hanyang to supervise the armies.
translations.idiomatic: Sidao himself then came from Hanyang to take command.

sentences.zh: 十一月，攻城急，城中死傷者至萬三千人。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the siege grew urgent; dead and wounded in the city reached thirteen thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the assault intensified, and dead and wounded in the city rose to thirteen thousand.

sentences.zh: 似道乃密遣宋京詣軍中請稱臣，輸歲幣，不從。

translations.literal: Sidao thereupon secretly sent Song Jing to the [Yuan] camp to request that [Song] call itself a vassal and pay annual tribute; [the Yuan side] would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Sidao secretly sent Song Jing to the Yuan camp to offer submission and annual tribute, but they refused.

sentences.zh: 會憲宗皇帝晏駕于釣魚山，合州守王堅使阮思聰踔急流走報鄂，似道再遣京議歲幣，遂許之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianzong of Yuan died at Diaoyu Mountain, Wang Jian the Prefect of Hezhou had Ruan Sicong cross the rapids in haste to run and report to Ezhou. Sidao again sent Jing to negotiate the annual tribute, and they thereupon agreed.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianzong died at Diaoyu Mountain, Hezhou Prefect Wang Jian sent Ruan Sicong racing through the rapids to bring word to Ezhou. Sidao again sent Song Jing to negotiate tribute, and this time they agreed.

sentences.zh: 大元兵拔砦而北，留張傑、閻旺以偏師候湖南兵。

translations.literal: Great Yuan troops pulled up their camps and went north, leaving Zhang Jie and Yan Wang with a detached force to wait for Hunan troops.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Yuan army broke camp and marched north, leaving Zhang Jie and Yan Wang with a detached force to watch for Hunan troops.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，兵至，傑作浮梁新生磯，濟師北歸。

translations.literal: In the first month of the next year the troops arrived. Jie built a pontoon bridge at Xinsheng Ji and crossed the army to return north.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year the troops arrived. Zhang Jie built a pontoon bridge at Xinsheng Ji and ferried the army back north.

sentences.zh: 似道用劉整計，攻斷浮梁，殺殿兵百七十，遂上表以肅清聞。

translations.literal: Sidao used Liu Zheng's plan to attack and cut the pontoon bridge, killing one hundred and seventy rearguard troops. He thereupon submitted a memorial reporting complete pacification.
translations.idiomatic: Following Liu Zheng's plan, Sidao attacked and severed the pontoon bridge, killing a hundred and seventy rearguard troops. He then memorialized the throne that the enemy had been completely cleared away.

sentences.zh: 帝以其有再造功，以少傅、右丞相召入朝，百官郊勞如文彥博故事。

translations.literal: The emperor, because he had the merit of restoring [the dynasty], summoned him to court as Junior Mentor and Right Chief Councillor; all officials welcomed him in the suburbs according to the precedent of Wen Yanzuo.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor credited him with having saved the dynasty, summoned him to court as junior mentor and right chief councillor, and had all officials welcome him in the suburbs by the precedent set for Wen Yanzuo.

sentences.zh: 初，似道在漢陽，時丞相吳潛用監察御史饒應子言，移之黃州，而分曹世雄等兵以屬江閫。

translations.literal: Initially, when Sidao was at Hanyang, Chief Councillor Wu Qian at that time, using Supervising Censor Rao Yingzi's advice, moved him to Huangzhou, and divided Cao Shixiong's troops and others to belong to the Jiang military commission.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Sidao was at Hanyang, Chief Councillor Wu Qian, acting on Supervising Censor Rao Yingzi's advice, transferred him to Huangzhou and reassigned Cao Shixiong's troops and others to the Jiang military command.

sentences.zh: 黃雖下流，實兵沖。

translations.literal: Although Huang [Zhou] was downstream, it was in truth a military choke point.
translations.idiomatic: Huangzhou lay downstream, but it was a critical military position.

sentences.zh: 似道以為潛欲殺己，銜之。

translations.literal: Sidao thought Qian intended to kill him and harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Sidao believed Qian meant to destroy him and nursed a deep grudge.

sentences.zh: 且聞潛事急時，每事先發後奏；

translations.literal: Moreover he heard that when Qian faced emergencies, he always acted first and reported afterward;
translations.idiomatic: He also heard that in emergencies Wu Qian always acted first and reported afterward;

sentences.zh: 帝欲立榮王子孟啟為太子，潛又不可。

translations.literal: when the emperor wished to establish Prince Rong's son Meng Qi as heir apparent, Qian again objected.
translations.idiomatic: and that when the emperor wished to make Prince Rong's son Meng Qi heir apparent, Qian had again objected.

sentences.zh: 帝已積怒潛，似道遂陳建儲之策，令沈炎劾潛措置無方，致全、衡、永、桂皆破，大稱旨。

translations.literal: The emperor had already accumulated anger toward Qian. Sidao thereupon presented a plan for establishing the heir, had Shen Yan impeach Qian for mismanagement that caused Quan, Heng, Yong, and Gui all to fall—greatly pleasing the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor already harbored deep anger toward Qian. Sidao then proposed a plan to establish the heir, had Shen Yan impeach Qian for mismanagement that had led to the fall of Quan, Heng, Yong, and Gui—and won the emperor's full approval.

sentences.zh: 乃議立孟啟，貶潛循州，盡逐其黨人。

translations.literal: Thereupon they deliberated establishing Meng Qi [as heir], demoted Qian to Xunzhou, and completely drove out his faction.
translations.idiomatic: They then resolved to install Meng Qi as heir, banished Qian to Xunzhou, and drove out all his followers.

sentences.zh: 高達在圍中，恃其武勇，殊易似道，每見其督戰，即戲之曰：「巍巾者何能為哉！

translations.literal: Gao Da, within the siege, relied on his martial valor and treated Sidao with contempt. Whenever he saw him supervising battle, he would mock him, saying: "What can a man in a gauze cap do!"
translations.idiomatic: Gao Da, inside the siege lines, counted on his martial prowess and held Sidao in contempt. Whenever he saw Sidao directing the battle, he would mock him: "What can a man in a scholar's cap do!"

sentences.zh: 」每戰，必須勞始出，否即使兵士嘩于其門。

translations.literal: Before each battle he had to be coaxed before he would come out; otherwise he would have soldiers clamor at his gate.
translations.idiomatic: Before every battle he had to be coaxed before he would come out; otherwise he set his soldiers to clamor at Sidao's gate.

sentences.zh: 呂文德諂似道，即使人呵曰：「宣撫在，何敢爾邪！

translations.literal: Lü Wende flattered Sidao and had someone shout: "The Pacification Commissioner is here—how dare you act thus!"
translations.idiomatic: Lü Wende flattered Sidao and had a man shout, "The pacification commissioner is present—how dare you behave like this!"

sentences.zh: 」曹世雄、向士璧在軍中，事皆不關白似道，故似道皆恨之。

translations.literal: Cao Shixiong and Xiang Shibi were in the army; matters did not need to be reported to Sidao—therefore Sidao resented them all.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Shixiong and Xiang Shibi were in the army and handled matters without reporting to Sidao, so he resented them both.

sentences.zh: 以核諸兵費，世雄、士璧皆坐侵盜官錢貶遠州。

translations.literal: On the pretext of auditing military expenses, Shixiong and Shibi were both sentenced for embezzling official funds and demoted to distant prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: On the pretext of auditing military expenses, Shixiong and Shibi were both convicted of embezzling public funds and banished to distant prefectures.

sentences.zh: 每言于帝欲誅達，帝知其有功，不從。

translations.literal: He repeatedly told the emperor he wanted to execute Da; the emperor knew Da had merit and did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly urged the emperor to execute Gao Da, but the emperor knew Da's worth and refused.

sentences.zh: 尋論功，以文德為第一，而達居其次。

translations.literal: Soon when distributing merit, Wende was ranked first and Da second.
translations.idiomatic: When rewards were later assigned, Wende was ranked first and Da second.

sentences.zh: 明年，大元世祖皇帝登極，遣翰林侍讀學士、國信使郝經等持書申好息兵，且征歲幣。

translations.literal: The next year Emperor Shizu of Great Yuan ascended the throne and dispatched Academician Reader of the Hanlin Academy and National Emissary Hao Jing and others with a letter to renew friendship and cease warfare, and also to collect the annual tribute.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the Great Yuan emperor Kublai ascended the throne and sent Hanlin academician reader and national emissary Hao Jing and others with a letter offering friendship, calling for a halt to war, and demanding the annual tribute.

sentences.zh: 似道方使廖瑩中輩撰《福華編》稱頌鄂功，通國皆不知所謂和也。

translations.literal: Sidao was then having Liao Yingzhong and others compile the *Fuhua Bian* praising the achievements at Ezhou; the whole realm did not know what was meant by peace.
translations.idiomatic: Sidao meanwhile had Liao Yingzhong and others compile the *Fuhua Bian* to glorify the victory at Ezhou, and the whole realm knew nothing of any peace settlement.

sentences.zh: 似道乃密令淮東制置司拘經等於真州忠勇軍營。

translations.literal: Sidao thereupon secretly ordered the Huai East Military Commission to detain Jing and the others at the Loyal and Brave Army camp at Zhenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Sidao then secretly ordered the Huai East military commission to detain Hao Jing and his party at the Loyal and Brave Army camp in Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 時理宗在位久，內侍董宋臣、盧允升為之聚斂以媚之。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Lizong had held the throne for a long time. The eunuchs Dong Songchen and Lu Yunsheng amassed wealth for him to win his favor.
translations.idiomatic: By then Emperor Lizong had reigned for many years, and the eunuchs Dong Songchen and Lu Yunsheng amassed wealth to please him.

sentences.zh: 引薦奔競之士，交通賄賂，置諸通顯。

translations.literal: They recommended ambitious schemers, exchanged bribes, and placed them in high and prominent posts.
translations.idiomatic: They promoted ambitious schemers, traded in bribes, and placed them in high office.

sentences.zh: 又用外戚子弟為監司、郡守。

translations.literal: They also used sons and nephews of imperial affinal kin as circuit intendants and prefects.
translations.idiomatic: They also installed sons and nephews of the imperial in-laws as circuit intendants and prefects.

sentences.zh: 作芙蓉閣、香蘭亭宮中，進倡優傀儡，以奉帝為游燕。

translations.literal: They built the Furong Pavilion and Xianglan Pavilion in the palace, presented singing girls and puppet players, and served the emperor in leisurely pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: They built the Furong Pavilion and Xianglan Pavilion within the palace, supplied singers, actors, and puppet players, and kept the emperor supplied with amusements.

sentences.zh: 竊弄權柄。

translations.literal: They secretly wielded power.
translations.idiomatic: They wielded power behind the throne.

sentences.zh: 台臣有言之者，帝宣諭去之，謂之「節貼」。

translations.literal: When censorial officials spoke of them, the emperor would issue an edict of instruction to remove them, calling it "jie tie."
translations.idiomatic: When censors spoke against them, the emperor would issue an admonitory edict for their removal—a procedure called "jie tie."

sentences.zh: 似道入，逐盧、董所薦林光世等，悉罷之，勒外戚不得為監司、郡守，子弟門客斂跡，不敢幹朝政。

translations.literal: When Sidao entered [office], he drove out those recommended by Lu and Dong such as Lin Guangshi and dismissed them all; he forbade imperial affinal kin from serving as circuit intendants and prefects; sons, nephews, and retainers restrained themselves and did not dare meddle in court affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Sidao came to power, he drove out Lu and Dong's protégés such as Lin Guangshi and dismissed them all. He forbade imperial in-laws from serving as circuit intendants or prefects, and their sons, nephews, and clients withdrew and dared not meddle in government.

sentences.zh: 由是權傾中外，進用群小。

translations.literal: From this his power tilted toward inside and outside; he promoted and employed petty men.
translations.idiomatic: From then on his authority dominated court and country alike, and he filled office with petty men.

sentences.zh: 取先朝舊法，率意紛更，增吏部七司法。

translations.literal: He took old laws of former dynasties and according to whim changed them in confusion, adding seven new laws to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He took the laws of earlier reigns and altered them at will, adding seven new statutes to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 買公田以罷和糴，浙西田畝有直千緡者，似道均以四十緡買之。

translations.literal: He bought public fields to abolish the tax-in-kind grain purchase system. In western Zhejiang there were fields worth a thousand strings per mu; Sidao uniformly bought them at forty strings each.
translations.idiomatic: He purchased public fields to abolish the state grain-purchase system. In western Zhejiang some fields were worth a thousand strings per mu, yet Sidao bought them all at a flat forty strings.

sentences.zh: 數稍多，予銀絹；

translations.literal: When the quantity was somewhat large, they were given silver and silk;
translations.idiomatic: When the amount was somewhat larger, payment was made in silver and silk;

sentences.zh: 又多，予度牒告身。

translations.literal: When the quantity was even greater, they were given ordination certificates and appointment documents.
translations.idiomatic: When the amount was still larger, payment was made in ordination certificates and official appointment documents.

sentences.zh: 吏又恣為操切，浙中大擾。

translations.literal: The officials again acted arbitrarily with harsh enforcement, and central Zhejiang was greatly disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: Officials once again enforced the policy with arbitrary harshness, throwing central Zhejiang into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 有奉行不至者，提領劉良貴劾之。

translations.literal: Those who did not fully carry out the policy were impeached by the superintendent Liu Lianggui.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who failed to implement the policy fully was impeached by Liu Lianggui, the superintendent in charge.

sentences.zh: 有司爭相迎合，務以買田多為功，皆繆以七八斗為石。

translations.literal: The responsible officials competed to curry favor, striving to take buying much land as merit; all falsely reckoned seven or eight pecks as a shi.
translations.idiomatic: Local officials vied to ingratiate themselves, treating how much land they purchased as their measure of achievement—and all of them fraudulently counted seven or eight pecks as a full shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 其後，田少與磽瘠、虧租與佃人負租而逃者，率取償田主。

translations.literal: Afterward, when the fields were scarce and barren and poor, or when rent was deficient and tenant farmers fled owing rent, as a rule compensation was exacted from the landowner.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when purchased fields proved too small or too barren, or when rents fell short and tenant farmers fled leaving unpaid rent, the landowner was invariably forced to make up the difference.

sentences.zh: 六郡之民，破家者多。

translations.literal: Among the people of the six prefectures, many had their families ruined.
translations.idiomatic: In the six prefectures, countless families were driven to ruin.

sentences.zh: 包恢知平江，督買田。

translations.literal: Bao Hui served as prefect of Pingjiang and supervised the purchase of fields.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Hui, as prefect of Pingjiang, supervised the land purchases.

sentences.zh: 至以肉刑從事。

translations.literal: He went so far as to apply corporal punishment in the work.
translations.idiomatic: He even resorted to corporal punishment to enforce the policy.

sentences.zh: 復以楮賤作銀關，以一準十八界會之三，自製其印文如「賈」字狀行之，十七界廢不用。

translations.literal: Again, because paper currency was cheap, he made silver notes, using one to equal three of the eighteenth issue of huizi; he fashioned the seal inscription himself in the form of the character "Jia" and put them into circulation; the seventeenth issue was abolished and no longer used.
translations.idiomatic: Because paper notes had depreciated, he also introduced silver certificates, valuing each at three notes from the eighteenth huizi issue. He designed the seal himself in the shape of the character "Jia" and put the new notes into circulation; the seventeenth issue was abolished.

sentences.zh: 銀關行，物價益踴，楮益賤。

translations.literal: When the silver notes circulated, prices rose even more steeply, and paper currency became even cheaper.
translations.idiomatic: Once the silver certificates were in circulation, prices surged still higher and paper money sank even further in value.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，彗出柳，光燭天，長數十丈，自四更見東方，日高始滅。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn, a comet appeared in Willow; its light illuminated the sky, tens of zhang in length; from the fourth watch it was seen in the east, and only when the sun was high did it disappear.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, a comet appeared in the Willow constellation, blazing across the heavens for dozens of zhang. Visible in the east from the fourth watch, it did not fade until the sun stood high.

sentences.zh: 台諫、布韋皆上書，言此公田不便，民間愁怨所致。

translations.literal: Censorial remonstrators and commoners all submitted memorials, saying this was because the public-field policy was inconvenient and had caused popular grief and resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Censors, remonstrators, and commoners alike submitted memorials, attributing the omen to the burdensome public-field policy and the popular misery and resentment it had provoked.

sentences.zh: 似道上書力辯之，且乞罷政。

translations.literal: Sidao submitted a memorial vigorously arguing against this and also begged to resign from government.
translations.idiomatic: Sidao submitted a memorial forcefully rebutting the charge and asked to resign his post.

sentences.zh: 帝勉留之曰；

translations.literal: The emperor urged him to stay, saying:
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pressed him to remain and said:

sentences.zh: 「公田不可行，卿建議之始，朕已沮之矣。

translations.literal: "The public-field policy must not be abandoned. When you first proposed it, I had already checked those who would have stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: "The public-field policy cannot be abandoned. When you first proposed it, I had already held back those who would have blocked it.

sentences.zh: 今公私兼裕，一歲軍餉，皆仰於此。

translations.literal: Now both public and private are abundantly provided for; a year's military rations all depend on this.
translations.idiomatic: Public and private coffers alike are now flush, and the whole year's military provisions depend on this policy.

sentences.zh: 使因人言而罷之，雖足以快一時之議，如國計何！

translations.literal: If we abandon it because of what people say, although that may satisfy momentary opinion, what of the state plan!
translations.idiomatic: If we abandon it because of public clamor, we may appease opinion for the moment—but what then becomes of the state's finances?

sentences.zh: 」有太學生蕭規、葉李等上書，言似道專政。

translations.literal: " Imperial Academy students Xiao Gui, Ye Li, and others submitted memorials saying Sidao monopolized government.
translations.idiomatic: " Imperial Academy students such as Xiao Gui and Ye Li submitted memorials accusing Sidao of monopolizing power.

sentences.zh: 命京尹劉良貴捃摭以罪，悉黥配之。

translations.literal: He ordered Capital Magistrate Liu Lianggui to gather and fabricate crimes against them; all were tattooed and banished.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Capital Magistrate Liu Lianggui to scrape together charges against them; all were tattooed and exiled.

sentences.zh: 後又行推排法。

translations.literal: Later the land reassessment and registration method was also implemented.
translations.idiomatic: Later he also implemented the land reassessment policy.

sentences.zh: 江南之地，尺寸皆有稅，而民力弊矣。

translations.literal: In the Jiangnan region, every inch of land had taxation, and the people's strength was exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiangnan, even the smallest patch of ground carried a tax burden, and popular resources were utterly spent.

sentences.zh: 理宗崩，度宗又其所立，每朝必答拜，稱之曰「師臣」而不名，朝臣皆稱為「周公」。

translations.literal: When Lizong died, Duzong was also one he had enthroned; at every court audience Duzong would return his bow, calling him "Master Minister" without using his name, and court officials all called him "the Duke of Zhou."
translations.idiomatic: When Lizong died, Duzong—whom Sidao had placed on the throne—would at every audience return his bow of respect, addressing him as "Master Minister" without speaking his name; court officials all called him "the Duke of Zhou."

sentences.zh: 甫葬理宗，即棄官去，使呂文德報北兵攻下沱急，朝中大駭，帝與太后手為詔起之。

translations.literal: Right after burying Lizong, he immediately abandoned his office and left; he had Lü Wende report that northern troops were urgently attacking Xiatuo; the court was greatly alarmed; the emperor and empress dowager personally drafted an edict recalling him.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as Lizong was buried, he resigned and left office, then had Lü Wende report that northern forces were pressing urgently against Xiatuo. The court was thrown into panic, and the emperor and empress dowager personally drafted an edict summoning him back.

sentences.zh: 似道至，欲以經筵拜太師，以典故須建節，授鎮東軍節度使，似道怒曰：「節度使粗人之極致爾！

translations.literal: When Sidao arrived, he wished to be appointed Grand Preceptor through the classics lecture; according to precedent this required establishing a commandery standard; he was made military commissioner of the Zhendong Army. Sidao raged: "Military commissioner is only the ultimate rank for coarse men!
translations.idiomatic: When Sidao returned, he sought appointment as Grand Preceptor through the classics lecture; precedent required that such an appointment be accompanied by the bestowal of a commandery standard, so he was made military commissioner of the Zhendong Army. Sidao fumed: "Military commissioner is the highest rank a crude man can reach!

sentences.zh: 」遂命出節，都人聚觀。

translations.literal: " So he ordered the standard to be issued; the capital populace gathered to watch.
translations.idiomatic: " Nevertheless he ordered the standard issued, and the people of the capital crowded around to watch.

sentences.zh: 節已出，復曰：「時日不利。

translations.literal: The standard had already been issued, then he said again: "The day and hour are unpropitious.
translations.idiomatic: The standard had already been issued when he declared: "The day and hour are inauspicious.

sentences.zh: 」亟命返之。

translations.literal: " He urgently ordered it returned.
translations.idiomatic: " He immediately ordered it sent back.

sentences.zh: 宋制：節出，有撤關壞屋，無倒節理，以示不屈。

translations.literal: Song custom: when a standard was issued, some would demolish gates and ruin houses; there was no principle of reversing a standard—to show unyielding spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Under Song custom, when a commissioner received his standard, some would tear down gates or wreck buildings rather than let the standard pass reversed—there was no such thing as turning a standard back, for it symbolized resolute honor.

sentences.zh: 至是，人皆駭歎。

translations.literal: At this, everyone was shocked and sighing.
translations.idiomatic: At this, all who saw it were stunned and appalled.

sentences.zh: 然下沱之報實無兵也。

translations.literal: Yet in fact there were no troops in the report about Xiatuo.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the report of crisis at Xiatuo had been entirely false—there were no enemy troops at all.

sentences.zh: 三年，又乞歸養。

translations.literal: In the third year, he again requested leave to return home to care for his parents.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, he again asked to retire and return home to tend to his parents.

sentences.zh: 大臣、侍從傳旨留之者日四五至，中使加賜賚者日十數至，夜即交臥第外以守之。

translations.literal: Ministers and attendants conveying the edict to retain him came four or five times a day; palace envoys bringing additional gifts came more than ten times a day; at night they lay stacked outside his residence to guard him.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers and attendants bearing orders that he remain came four or five times daily; palace envoys bearing additional gifts arrived more than ten times a day; at night they lay stacked outside his gate to keep watch over him.

sentences.zh: 除太師、平章軍國重事，一月三赴經筵，三日一朝，赴中書堂治事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand Preceptor and Grand Controller of Military and State Affairs; three times a month he attended the classics lecture, once every three days he attended court, going to the Central Secretariat to handle affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Grand Preceptor and Director of Military and State Affairs, required to attend the classics lecture three times a month, hold audience once every three days, and preside at the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 賜第葛嶺，使迎養其中。

translations.literal: He was given a mansion at Geling, and his parents were brought to be cared for there.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted an estate at Geling, where his parents were installed for him to support in comfort.

sentences.zh: 吏抱文書就第署，大小朝政，一切決于館客廖瑩中、堂吏翁應龍，宰執充位署紙尾而已。

translations.literal: Clerks carried documents to his residence for signing; all major and minor court affairs were decided entirely by his retainer Liao Yingzhong and secretarial clerk Weng Yinglong; the chief ministers merely filled positions and signed at the bottom of papers.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks brought documents to his residence for his signature; all affairs great and small were decided by his house guest Liao Yingzhong and chief clerk Weng Yinglong—the chief ministers were merely figureheads who signed their names at the foot of each document.

sentences.zh: 似道雖深居，凡台諫彈劾、諸司薦辟及京尹、畿漕一切事，不關白不敢行，李芾、文天祥、陳文龍、陸達、杜淵、張仲微、謝章輩，小忤意輒斥，重則屏棄之，終身不錄。

translations.literal: Although Sidao lived in seclusion, for all matters of censorial impeachment, recommendations and appointments by various offices, and everything involving the capital magistrate and metropolitan transport commissioners—none dared act without reporting to him. Li Fu, Wen Tianxiang, Chen Wenlong, Lu Da, Du Yuan, Zhang Zhongwei, Xie Zhang, and the like—if they slightly offended his wishes they were at once dismissed; if the offense was serious they were cast aside and never again recorded for office.
translations.idiomatic: Though Sidao kept to his residence, nothing could proceed without his approval—censorial impeachments, departmental recommendations and appointments, the capital magistrate, metropolitan transport commissioners, all of it. Li Fu, Wen Tianxiang, Chen Wenlong, Lu Da, Du Yuan, Zhang Zhongwei, Xie Zhang, and others who crossed him even slightly were promptly dismissed; serious offenders were permanently banished from office.

sentences.zh: 一時正人端士，為似道破壞殆盡。

translations.literal: For a time upright and principled men were nearly all destroyed by Sidao.
translations.idiomatic: In that period, upright and principled officials were nearly all driven out by Sidao.

sentences.zh: 吏爭納賂求美職，其求為帥閫、監司、郡守者，貢獻不可勝計。

translations.literal: Officials competed to pay bribes seeking fine posts; those who sought to become commanders, circuit intendants, and prefects offered tribute beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Officials scrambled to buy their way into desirable posts; those seeking commands, circuit intendancies, and prefectures offered tribute beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 趙氵晉輩爭獻寶玉，陳奕至以兄事似道之玉工陳振民以求進，一時貪風大肆。

translations.literal: Zhao Jin and his ilk competed to present precious jades; Chen Yi went so far as to treat Sidao's jade craftsman Chen Zhenmin as an elder brother to seek advancement; for a time the wind of greed ran rampant.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Jin and others vied to present precious jades; Chen Yi even treated Sidao's jade craftsman Chen Zhenmin as an elder brother to win advancement. Greed ran rampant throughout the court.

sentences.zh: 五年，復稱疾求去。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he again claimed illness and requested to leave.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, he again pleaded illness and asked to resign.

sentences.zh: 帝泣涕留之，不從。

translations.literal: The emperor wept and tearfully urged him to stay; he would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wept and begged him to stay, but Sidao would not agree.

sentences.zh: 令六日一朝，一月兩赴經筵。

translations.literal: He was ordered to attend court once every six days and the classics lecture twice a month.
translations.idiomatic: He was permitted to attend court once every six days and the classics lecture twice a month.

sentences.zh: 六年，命入朝不拜。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he was ordered that when entering court he need not bow.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, he was granted exemption from bowing when entering court.

sentences.zh: 朝退，帝必起避席，目送之出殿廷始坐。

translations.literal: When court was dismissed, the emperor always rose and moved from his seat, watching with his eyes until Sidao left the hall before sitting down again.
translations.idiomatic: When court adjourned, the emperor always rose from his seat and watched Sidao leave the hall before sitting down again.

sentences.zh: 繼又令十日一入朝。

translations.literal: Subsequently he was again ordered to enter court once every ten days.
translations.idiomatic: He was later permitted to attend court only once every ten days.

sentences.zh: 時襄陽圍已急，似道日坐葛嶺，起樓閣亭榭，取宮人娼尼有美色者為妾，日淫樂其中。

translations.literal: At that time the siege of Xiangyang was already urgent, yet Sidao sat daily at Geling, erecting towers, pavilions, and terraces; he took palace women and courtesan nuns of beautiful appearance as concubines and daily indulged in licentious pleasure there.
translations.idiomatic: While the siege of Xiangyang grew ever more desperate, Sidao passed his days at Geling, building towers and pavilions, taking beautiful palace women and courtesan nuns as concubines, and indulging in debauchery.

sentences.zh: 惟故博徒日至縱博，人無敢窺其第者。

translations.literal: Only former gamblers came daily to gamble freely; no one dared peep into his residence.
translations.idiomatic: Only his old gambling companions came daily to wager with him, and no one dared pry into his estate.

sentences.zh: 其妾有兄來，立府門，若將入者，似道見之，縛投火中。

translations.literal: One of his concubines had a brother who came and stood at the mansion gate as if about to enter; when Sidao saw him, he had him bound and thrown into a fire.
translations.idiomatic: When a concubine's brother appeared at the gate as though about to enter, Sidao had him bound and thrown into a fire.

sentences.zh: 嘗與群妾踞地鬥蟋蟀，所狎客入，戲之曰：「此軍國重事邪？

translations.literal: Once, squatting on the ground with his concubines fighting crickets, a favorite guest entered and joked: "Is this a weighty affair of state and army?
translations.idiomatic: Once, while squatting on the ground with his concubines pitting crickets against each other, a favorite guest entered and teased him: "Is this the weighty business of state you were appointed to manage?

sentences.zh: 」酷嗜寶玩，建多寶閣，日一登玩。

translations.literal: " He was passionately fond of precious curios; he built a Hall of Many Treasures and climbed it daily to admire them.
translations.idiomatic: " He was obsessed with precious curios, built a Hall of Many Treasures, and climbed to admire his collection every day.

sentences.zh: 聞餘疴有玉帶，求之，已徇葬矣，發其塚取之。

translations.literal: Hearing that Yu Ke had a jade belt, he sought it; it had already been buried with him, so he opened the tomb and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Yu Ke had owned a jade belt, he demanded it; told it had already been buried with its owner, he opened the tomb and took it.

sentences.zh: 人有物，求不予，輒得罪。

translations.literal: If someone had an object and, when asked, did not give it, he would at once fall into disgrace.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who refused to surrender a coveted object would immediately fall from favor.

sentences.zh: 自是，或累月不朝，帝如景靈宮亦不從駕。

translations.literal: From this, he sometimes went months without attending court; when the emperor went to the Jingling Palace he also did not accompany the procession.
translations.idiomatic: After this he sometimes went months without attending court, and when the emperor visited the Jingling Palace he did not accompany the imperial procession.

sentences.zh: 八年，明堂禮成，祀景靈宮。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, when the Bright Hall rites were completed, the emperor sacrificed at the Jingling Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, after the Bright Hall rites were completed, the emperor proceeded to sacrifice at the Jingling Palace.

sentences.zh: 天大雨，似道期帝雨止升輅。

translations.literal: Heaven sent great rain; Sidao expected the emperor to wait until the rain stopped before mounting the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Rain fell in torrents, and Sidao expected the emperor to wait until it stopped before mounting the imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 胡貴嬪之父顯祖為帶禦器械，請如開禧故事，卻輅，乘逍遙輦還宮，帝曰平章云云，顯祖紿曰：「平章已允乘逍遙輦矣。

translations.literal: Hu Guibin's father Xianzu served as director of the imperial armory; he requested that, following the Kaixi precedent, the carriage be turned back and the emperor return to the palace in the leisurely palanquin. The emperor said the chief minister had said such and such; Xianzu deceived him: "The chief minister has already agreed that you may ride the leisurely palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Guibin's father Xianzu, director of the imperial armory, asked that following the Kaixi precedent the imperial carriage be turned back and the emperor return to the palace in a covered palanquin. When the emperor said he must consult the chief minister, Xianzu lied: "The chief minister has already approved the palanquin.

sentences.zh: 」帝遂歸。

translations.literal: " The emperor then returned.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor then returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 似道大怒曰：「臣為大禮使，陛下舉動不得預聞，乞罷政。

translations.literal: Sidao was greatly enraged and said: "I serve as commissioner for the great rites; Your Majesty's movements were not reported to me beforehand. I beg to resign from government.
translations.idiomatic: Sidao flew into a rage: "As commissioner for the great rites, I was not informed of Your Majesty's movements in advance. I beg to resign.

sentences.zh: 」即日出嘉會門，帝留之不得，乃罷顯祖，涕泣出貴嬪為尼，始還。

translations.literal: " That same day he went out through the Jiahui Gate; the emperor could not retain him, so he dismissed Xianzu, tearfully sent Guibin out to become a nun, and only then did Sidao return.
translations.idiomatic: " That same day he left through the Jiahui Gate. Unable to keep him, the emperor dismissed Xianzu, weeping as he sent Guibin away to become a nun—only then did Sidao return.

sentences.zh: 似道既專恣日甚，畏人議己，務以權術駕馭，不愛官爵，牢籠一時名士，又加太學餐錢，寬科場恩例，以小利啖之。

translations.literal: As Sidao's monopoly and arrogance grew daily, fearing that people would criticize him, he strove to control others through power and stratagem; he did not begrudge offices and ranks, drawing in famous scholars of the time; he also increased Imperial Academy meal stipends and relaxed examination favor policies, baiting them with small benefits.
translations.idiomatic: As Sidao's monopoly of power grew ever bolder, fearing criticism he relied on manipulation and stratagem. He lavished offices and ranks to win over leading scholars, increased Imperial Academy stipends, and relaxed examination privileges—dangling small favors to keep them quiet.

sentences.zh: 由是言路斷絕，威福肆行。

translations.literal: From this the avenue of speech was cut off, and authority and favor ran unchecked.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the channels of remonstrance were sealed off, and he wielded power without restraint.

sentences.zh: 自圍襄陽以來，每上書請行邊，而陰使台諫上章留己。

translations.literal: Since the siege of Xiangyang began, he repeatedly submitted memorials requesting to go to the frontier, while secretly having censorial remonstrators submit chapters to retain him.
translations.idiomatic: Since the siege of Xiangyang began, he repeatedly memorialized asking to take command on the frontier, while secretly arranging for censors and remonstrators to submit memorials urging him to remain.

sentences.zh: 呂文煥以急告，似道復申請之，事下公卿雜議。

translations.literal: Lü Wenhuan reported urgency; Sidao again applied for permission; the matter was sent down for mixed deliberation among the chief ministers and nobles.
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Wenhuan sent urgent reports, Sidao again petitioned to take the field, and the matter was referred to the chief ministers for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 監察御史陳堅等以為師臣出，顧襄未必能及淮，顧淮未必能及襄，不若居中以運天下為得。

translations.literal: Supervising Censor Chen Jian and others held that if the Master Minister went out, looking to Xiang he might not be able also to reach the Huai, and looking to the Huai he might not be able also to reach Xiang; it was better to remain at the center and move the realm—that was the right course.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Censor Chen Jian and others argued that if the Master Minister left the capital, he could not simultaneously rescue Xiangyang and hold the Huai line; it was better to remain at the center and direct affairs from there.

sentences.zh: 乃就中書置機速房以調邊事。

translations.literal: Thereupon at the Central Secretariat they established an Expedited Affairs Office to coordinate frontier matters.
translations.idiomatic: An Expedited Affairs Office was therefore set up within the Central Secretariat to coordinate frontier operations.

sentences.zh: 時物議多言高達可援襄陽者，監察御史李旺率朝士入言於似道。

translations.literal: At the time public opinion widely said Gao Da could relieve Xiangyang; Supervising Censor Li Wang led court officials in to speak to Sidao.
translations.idiomatic: Public opinion at the time held that Gao Da could relieve Xiangyang; Supervising Censor Li Wang led a group of court officials to press this on Sidao.

sentences.zh: 似道曰：「吾用達，如呂氏何？

translations.literal: Sidao said: "If I employ Da, what of the Lü family?
translations.idiomatic: Sidao replied: "If I appoint Gao Da, what becomes of the Lü family?

sentences.zh: 」旺等出，歎曰：「呂氏安則趙氏危矣。

translations.literal: " When Wang and the others came out, they sighed: "If the Lü family is secure, the Zhao house is in peril.
translations.idiomatic: " As they left, Wang and the others sighed: "When the Lü family is secure, the Zhao dynasty is in danger.

sentences.zh: 」文煥在襄，聞達且入援，亦不樂，以語其客。

translations.literal: " Wenhuan was at Xiang; hearing that Da was about to enter as relief, he was also displeased and spoke of it to his guest.
translations.idiomatic: " At Xiangyang, Wenhuan heard that Gao Da was to be sent as relief and was displeased; he confided as much to a guest.

sentences.zh: 客曰：「易耳，今朝廷以襄陽急，故遣達援之，吾以捷聞，則達必不成遣矣。

translations.literal: The guest said: "Easy. Now the court, because Xiangyang is urgent, therefore sends Da to relieve it; if we report victory, then Da will certainly not be dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: His guest said: "That is easily solved. The court is sending Gao Da only because Xiangyang is desperate. Report a victory, and the dispatch will certainly be canceled.

sentences.zh: 」文煥大以為然。

translations.literal: " Wenhuan greatly agreed.
translations.idiomatic: " Wenhuan thought this excellent advice.

sentences.zh: 時襄兵出，獲哨騎數人，即繆以大捷奏，然不知朝中實無援襄事也。

translations.literal: At that time Xiangyang troops went out and captured several scout riders; they at once falsely reported a great victory, yet they did not know that in court there was in fact no plan to relieve Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangyang troops sallied forth, captured several enemy scouts, and immediately reported a great victory— unaware that the court had never intended to send relief at all.

sentences.zh: 襄陽降，似道曰：「臣始屢請行邊，先帝皆不之許，向使早聽臣出，當不至此爾。」

translations.literal: When Xiangyang surrendered, Sidao said: "Your servant repeatedly requested to go to the frontier; the late emperor never approved. If he had earlier listened and let me go out, it would not have come to this."
translations.idiomatic: When Xiangyang fell, Sidao said: "I repeatedly asked to take the field, but the late emperor never permitted it. Had he listened to me sooner, things would never have come to this."

sentences.zh: 十月，其母胡氏薨，詔以天子鹵簿葬之，起墳擬山陵，百官奉襄事，立大雨中，終日無敢易位。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, his mother Lady Hu died; an edict ordered her buried with the emperor's full guard of honor; the tomb mound was raised to resemble an imperial mausoleum; all officials attended the funeral rites, standing in heavy rain; for the whole day none dared shift position.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month his mother Lady Hu died. An edict granted her burial with the full imperial guard of honor; the tomb mound was built to rival an imperial mausoleum. Officials stood in pouring rain throughout the funeral rites, and for the entire day none dared move from his place.

sentences.zh: 尋起復入朝。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was recalled from mourning and reentered court.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled from mourning and returned to court.

sentences.zh: 度宗崩。

translations.literal: Duzong died.
translations.idiomatic: Duzong died.

sentences.zh: 大兵破鄂，太學諸生亦群言非師臣親出不可。

translations.literal: The great army captured E; Imperial Academy students also collectively said that unless the Master Minister personally went out, it would not do.
translations.idiomatic: When the main Mongol force took Ezhou, Imperial Academy students also clamored that only the Master Minister's personal command would suffice.

sentences.zh: 似道不得已，始開都督府臨安，然憚劉整，不行。

translations.literal: Sidao, having no choice, finally opened a commander-in-chief's headquarters at Lin'an, yet fearing Liu Zheng, he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Sidao, left no alternative, finally established a commander-in-chief's headquarters at Lin'an—but fearing Liu Zheng, he did not take the field himself.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，整死，似道欣然曰：「吾得天助也。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year, Zheng died; Sidao said with delight: "Heaven aids me.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year Liu Zheng died. Sidao exulted: "Heaven is on my side.

sentences.zh: 」乃上表出師，抽諸路精兵以行，金帛輜重之舟，舳臚相銜百餘里。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he submitted a memorial to take the army out; he drew elite troops from all circuits to march; boats of gold, silk, and baggage train linked stem to stern for more than a hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: " He then memorialized to take command in person, mustering elite troops from every circuit. Ships laden with gold, silk, and baggage stretched stem to stern for more than a hundred li.

sentences.zh: 至安吉，似道所乘舟膠堰中，劉師勇以千人入水曳之不能動，乃易他舟而去。

translations.literal: Reaching Anji, the boat Sidao rode stuck fast in a sluice; Liu Shiyong with a thousand men entered the water to drag it but could not move it; he then changed to another boat and left.
translations.idiomatic: At Anji, Sidao's boat stuck fast in a sluice gate. Liu Shiyong put a thousand men in the water to drag it free, but it would not budge; Sidao simply boarded another boat and sailed on.

sentences.zh: 至蕪湖，遣還軍中所俘曾安撫，以荔子、黃甘遺丞相伯顏，俾宋京如軍中，請輸歲幣稱臣如開慶約，不從。

translations.literal: Reaching Wuhu, he sent back Zeng Anfu, captured in the army; he sent lychees and yellow citrus as gifts to Chancellor Bayan; he had Song Jing go to the army to request paying annual tribute and submitting as vassal according to the Kaiqing agreement; Bayan did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: At Wuhu he released the captive Zeng Anfu, sent lychees and mandarin oranges as gifts to Chancellor Bayan, and dispatched Song Jing to the Mongol camp to offer annual tribute and vassal submission on the terms of the Kaiqing agreement. Bayan refused.

sentences.zh: 夏貴自合肥以師來會，袖中出編書示似道曰：「宋曆三百二十年。

translations.literal: Xia Gui came from Hefei with his army to join him; from his sleeve he produced a bound book and showed Sidao: "The Song dynasty has lasted three hundred and twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Gui marched from Hefei to join him, drew a bound chronology from his sleeve, and showed it to Sidao: "The Song dynasty has endured three hundred and twenty years.

sentences.zh: 」似道俯首而已。

translations.literal: " Sidao merely bowed his head.
translations.idiomatic: " Sidao could only bow his head in silence.

sentences.zh: 時一軍七萬餘人，盡屬孫虎臣，軍丁家洲。

translations.literal: At that time one army of more than seventy thousand men was entirely under Sun Huchen, encamped at Dingjiazhou.
translations.idiomatic: An army of more than seventy thousand men under Sun Huchen was encamped at Dingjiazhou.

sentences.zh: 似道與夏貴以少軍軍魯港。

translations.literal: Sidao and Xia Gui with a smaller army encamped at Lugang.
translations.idiomatic: Sidao and Xia Gui held Lugang with a smaller force.

sentences.zh: 二月庚申夜，虎臣以失利報，似道倉皇出，呼曰：「虎臣敗矣！

translations.literal: On the night of gengshen in the second month, Huchen reported defeat; Sidao rushed out in panic, crying: "Huchen is defeated!
translations.idiomatic: On the gengshen night of the second month, Huchen reported defeat. Sidao rushed out in panic, shouting: "Huchen is beaten!

sentences.zh: 」命召貴與計事。

translations.literal: " He ordered Gui summoned to consult on the affair.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered Xia Gui summoned to counsel on what to do.

sentences.zh: 頃之，虎臣至，撫膺而泣曰：「吾兵無一人用命也。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward Huchen arrived, clutched his chest and wept: "Not one of my soldiers obeyed orders.
translations.idiomatic: Huchen soon arrived, clutched his chest, and wept: "Not a single soldier obeyed orders.

sentences.zh: 」貴微笑曰：「吾嘗血戰當之矣。

translations.literal: " Gui smiled slightly: "I have already fought bloody battles to hold them off.
translations.idiomatic: " Xia Gui smiled faintly: "I have already fought them to a bloody standstill.

sentences.zh: 」似道曰：「計將安出？

translations.literal: " Sidao said: "What plan shall we produce?
translations.idiomatic: " Sidao asked: "What is your plan?

sentences.zh: 」貴曰：「諸軍已膽落，吾何以戰？

translations.literal: " Gui said: "The armies' courage is already gone; how can I fight?
translations.idiomatic: " Xia Gui said: "The troops have lost all heart. How can I fight?

sentences.zh: 公惟入揚州，招潰兵，迎駕海上，吾特以死守淮西爾。

translations.literal: Your lordship need only enter Yangzhou, gather the routed troops, and welcome the imperial carriage to the sea; I will merely hold west of the Huai to the death.
translations.idiomatic: Your Excellency should go to Yangzhou, rally the routed troops, and escort the emperor to sea. I will hold west of the Huai to the death.

sentences.zh: 」遂解舟去。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he cast off his boat and left.
translations.idiomatic: " With that he cast off and sailed away.

sentences.zh: 似道亦與虎臣以單舸奔揚州。

translations.literal: Sidao also, with Huchen in a single small boat, fled to Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Sidao fled to Yangzhou as well, sharing a single small boat with Huchen.

sentences.zh: 明日，敗兵蔽江而下，似道使人登岸揚旗招之，皆不至，有為惡語慢罵之者。

translations.literal: The next day, defeated soldiers covered the river flowing downstream; Sidao sent men ashore to raise flags and summon them; none came; some uttered foul abuse and insults.
translations.idiomatic: The next day routed soldiers filled the river downstream. Sidao sent men ashore to wave flags and summon them, but none came—some hurled curses and abuse instead.

sentences.zh: 乃檄列郡如海上迎駕，上書請遷都，列郡守於是皆遁，遂入揚州。

translations.literal: Thereupon he issued orders to the various prefectures to go to sea to welcome the imperial carriage; he submitted a memorial requesting transfer of the capital; the various prefects and magistrates thereupon all fled; he then entered Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered the prefectures to prepare to receive the emperor at sea and memorialized to move the capital. Prefects and magistrates throughout the region fled, and Sidao entered Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 陳宜中請誅似道，謝太后曰：「似道勤勞三朝，安忍以一朝之罪，失待大臣之禮。

translations.literal: Chen Yizhong requested that Sidao be executed; Empress Dowager Xie said: "Sidao has toiled through three reigns; how can we bear, because of one morning's offense, to fail in the courtesy due a great minister?
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yizhong urged that Sidao be executed. Empress Dowager Xie said: "Sidao has served faithfully through three reigns. How can we, for a single day's failure, abandon the courtesy owed a great minister?

sentences.zh: 」止罷平章、都督，予祠官。

translations.literal: " She only dismissed him from Grand Councillor and commander-in-chief, granting him a sinecure post.
translations.idiomatic: " She merely stripped him of his posts as Grand Councillor and commander-in-chief and granted him a ceremonial sinecure.

sentences.zh: 三月，除似道諸不恤民之政，放還諸竄謫人，復吳潛、向士璧等官，誅其幕官翁應龍，廖瑩中、王庭皆自殺。

translations.literal: In the third month, Sidao's various policies that did not care for the people were abolished; all those exiled and banished were released and returned; Wu Qian, Xiang Shibi, and others were restored to office; his staff officer Weng Yinglong was executed; Liao Yingzhong and Wang Ting both committed suicide.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Sidao's oppressive policies were abolished, exiles were recalled, Wu Qian and Xiang Shibi were restored to office, his chief clerk Weng Yinglong was executed, and Liao Yingzhong and Wang Ting both took their own lives.

sentences.zh: 潘文卿、季可、陳堅、徐卿孫皆似道鷹犬，至是交章劾之。

translations.literal: Pan Wenqing, Ji Ke, Chen Jian, and Xu Qingsun were all Sidao's henchmen; by this time they submitted successive memorials impeaching him.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Wenqing, Ji Ke, Chen Jian, and Xu Qingsun had all been Jia Sidao's henchmen; they now filed successive memorials impeaching him.

sentences.zh: 四月，高斯得乞誅似道，不從。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Gao Side asked that Sidao be executed; the request was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Gao Side petitioned for Jia Sidao's execution, but the court refused.

sentences.zh: 而似道亦自上表乞保全，乃命削三官，然尚居揚不歸。

translations.literal: Sidao also submitted a memorial asking to be spared; he was ordered stripped of three ranks, yet he still remained at Yangzhou and did not return.
translations.idiomatic: Sidao also memorialized begging to be spared. He was stripped of three ranks but still lingered at Yangzhou without returning.

sentences.zh: 五月，王氇龠論似道既不死忠，又不死孝，太皇太后乃詔似道歸終喪。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Wang Luyue argued that Sidao had neither died for loyalty nor died for filial piety; the grand empress dowager then ordered Sidao to return and complete the mourning period.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Wang Luyue argued that Sidao had shown neither loyalty to the state nor filial duty in mourning. The grand empress dowager then ordered him home to complete his mourning obligations.

sentences.zh: 七月，黃鏞、王應麟請移似道鄰州，不從。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Huang Yong and Wang Yinglin asked that Sidao be moved to a neighboring prefecture; the request was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Huang Yong and Wang Yinglin asked that Sidao be transferred to a neighboring prefecture, but the court refused.

sentences.zh: 王氇龠入見太后曰：「本朝權臣稔禍，未有如似道之烈者。

translations.literal: Wang Luyue entered to see the empress dowager and said, "Among powerful ministers of this dynasty who have accumulated calamity, none has been as fierce as Sidao.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Luyue went in to see the empress dowager and said, "Among the powerful ministers of our dynasty who have brought disaster on the state, none has been as ruinous as Jia Sidao.

sentences.zh: 縉紳草茅不知幾疏，陛下皆抑而不行，非惟付人言於不恤，何以謝天下！

translations.literal: Court and commoners alike have submitted who knows how many memorials, yet Your Majesty has suppressed them all and not acted—not only disregarding public opinion, but how can you answer to the realm!
translations.idiomatic: Officials and commoners alike have submitted countless memorials, yet Your Majesty has suppressed them all. You not only ignore public outrage—how can you answer to the empire!

sentences.zh: 」始徙似道婺州。

translations.literal: " Only then was Sidao transferred to Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: " Only then was Sidao banished to Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 婺人聞似道將至，率眾為露布逐之。

translations.literal: When the people of Wu heard that Sidao was coming, they gathered in crowds and posted public notices to drive him away.
translations.idiomatic: When the people of Wuzhou learned Sidao was coming, they rallied and posted public proclamations demanding his expulsion.

sentences.zh: 監察御史孫嶸叟等皆以為罰輕，言之不已。

translations.literal: Investigating censor Sun Rongsou and others all considered the punishment too light and spoke of it without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating censor Sun Rongsou and others protested that the punishment was too lenient and kept pressing the matter.

sentences.zh: 又徙建寧府。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Jianning Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred again to Jianning Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 翁合奏言：「建甯乃名儒朱熹故里，雖三尺童子粗知向方，聞似道來嘔惡，況見其人！

translations.literal: Weng He memorialized, saying, "Jianning is the old home of the renowned scholar Zhu Xi; even a child of three feet roughly knows what is right—hearing that Sidao is coming they vomit in disgust, how much more if they were to see the man!
translations.idiomatic: Weng He memorialized: "Jianning is the homeland of the great scholar Zhu Xi. Even children there know right from wrong—they retch at the news that Sidao is coming, let alone at the sight of him!

sentences.zh: 」時國子司業方應發權直舍人院，封還錄黃，乞竄似道廣南；

translations.literal: " At that time Fang Yingfa, vice director of the Directorate of Education, was acting head of the Academy of Scholarly Worthies; he returned the draft edict sealed shut and asked that Sidao be banished to the far south;
translations.idiomatic: " At that time Fang Yingfa of the Directorate of Education, acting head of the Academy of Scholarly Worthies, returned the draft edict unapproved and asked that Sidao be exiled to the far south;

sentences.zh: 中書舍人王應麟、給事中黃鏞亦言之，皆不從。

translations.literal: Drafting drafter Wang Yinglin and drafting reviewer Huang Yong also spoke on it; none of these were accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Drafting drafter Wang Yinglin and drafting reviewer Huang Yong spoke as well, but the court would not agree.

sentences.zh: 侍御史陳文龍乞俯從眾言，陳景行、徐直方、孫嶸叟及監察御史俞浙並上疏，於是始謫似道為高州團練使、循州安置，籍其家。

translations.literal: Attendant censor Chen Wenlong asked that public opinion be humbly followed; Chen Jingxing, Xu Zhifang, Sun Rongsou, and investigating censor Yu Zhe all submitted memorials; only then was Sidao demoted to regiment commander of Gaozhou and settled at Xunzhou, and his household property was registered.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant censor Chen Wenlong urged the court to heed public opinion. Chen Jingxing, Xu Zhifang, Sun Rongsou, and investigating censor Yu Zhe all memorialized. Only then was Sidao demoted to regiment commander of Gaozhou, settled at Xunzhou, and his property confiscated.

sentences.zh: 福王與芮素恨似道，募有能殺似道者使送之貶所，有縣尉鄭虎臣欣然請行。

translations.literal: Prince Fu, Zhao Rui, had long hated Sidao and recruited anyone who could kill Sidao to escort him to his place of banishment; the county lieutenant Zheng Huchen gladly volunteered to go.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Fu, Zhao Rui, had long hated Sidao and offered a reward for anyone who would kill him while escorting him to exile. County lieutenant Zheng Huchen eagerly volunteered.

sentences.zh: 似道行時，侍妾尚數十人，虎臣悉屏去，奪其寶玉，徹轎蓋，𣌈行秋日中，令舁轎夫唱杭州歌謔之，每名斥似道，辱之備至。

translations.literal: When Sidao was on the road he still had several tens of concubines in attendance; Huchen dismissed them all, seized his jewels, removed the sedan canopy, and made him walk in the autumn sun, ordering the sedan bearers to sing Hangzhou songs to mock him, each verse naming and reviling Sidao, humiliating him to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: On the road Sidao still had dozens of concubines in attendance. Huchen dismissed them all, seized his jewels, removed the sedan canopy, and forced him to walk in the autumn heat while the bearers sang Hangzhou street songs mocking him by name, humiliating him in every way.

sentences.zh: 似道至古寺中，壁有吳潛南行所題字，虎臣呼似道曰：「賈團練，吳丞相何以至此？

translations.literal: When Sidao reached an old temple, on the wall were characters inscribed by Wu Qian on his journey south. Huchen called to Sidao, "Regiment Commander Jia, how did Chancellor Wu come to be here?
translations.idiomatic: At an old temple Sidao found on the wall an inscription left by Wu Qian on his own journey south. Huchen called out, "Regiment Commander Jia—how did Chancellor Wu end up here?

sentences.zh: 」似道慚不能對。

translations.literal: " Sidao was ashamed and could not answer.
translations.idiomatic: " Sidao was ashamed and had no reply.

sentences.zh: 嶸叟、應麟奏似道家畜乘輿服御物，有反狀，乞斬之。

translations.literal: Rongsou and Yinglin memorialized that Sidao's household kept imperial carriage accoutrements and regalia, showing signs of rebellion, and asked that he be beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Rongsou and Wang Yinglin memorialized that Sidao's household possessed imperial carriage fittings and regalia suggestive of treason and asked that he be executed.

sentences.zh: 詔遣鞫問，未至。

translations.literal: An edict was issued ordering him brought back for interrogation, but it had not yet arrived.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered him brought back for interrogation, but it had not yet arrived.

sentences.zh: 八月，似道至漳州木綿庵，虎臣屢諷之自殺，不聽，曰：「太皇許我不死，有詔即死。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Sidao reached the Kapok Hermitage at Zhangzhou. Huchen repeatedly hinted that he should kill himself; Sidao would not listen and said, "The grand empress dowager promised I would not die; when there is an edict I will die.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Sidao reached the Kapok Hermitage in Zhangzhou. Huchen repeatedly urged him to take his own life. Sidao refused, saying, "The grand empress dowager promised I would not be killed. I will die only when there is an edict.

sentences.zh: 」虎臣曰：「吾為天下殺似道，雖死何憾？

translations.literal: " Huchen said, "I kill Sidao for the realm—what regret would I have even if I die?
translations.idiomatic: " Huchen said, "I am killing Sidao for the empire. What regret would I have even if I die for it?

sentences.zh: 」拉殺之。

translations.literal: " and dragged him to his death.
translations.idiomatic: He killed him on the spot.
